translations.literal: Volume 136
translations.idiomatic: Volume 136

sentences.zh: 【齊紀二】 起閼逢困敦，盡屠維大荒落，凡六年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 2] From Efou Kundun through Tuxi Dahuangluo, six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 2 (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元四八四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, the year 484 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi, corresponding to 484 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，以後將軍柳世隆為尚書右僕射；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Rear General Liu Shilong was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Rear General Liu Shilong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良為護軍將軍兼司徒，領兵置佐，鎮西州。

translations.literal: Prince Jingling of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, was made Protector-General of the Army and concurrently Minister over the Masses, with military staff appointed, garrisoning West Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling Xiao Ziliang was made Protector-General of the Army and concurrently Minister over the Masses; he took on military aides and garrisoned West Province.

sentences.zh: 子良少有清尚，傾意賓客，才俊之士，皆游集其門。

translations.literal: Ziliang from youth had pure and lofty tastes, devoted himself to guests, and men of talent all gathered at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ziliang had refined tastes and lavished attention on his guests; talented men of every sort flocked to his house.

sentences.zh: 開西邸，多聚古人器服以充之。

translations.literal: He opened the Western Lodge and gathered many ancient vessels and vestments to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Western Lodge and filled it with antiquities—vessels and vestments from former ages.

sentences.zh: 記室參軍范雲、蕭琛、樂安任昉、法曹參軍王融、衛軍東閣祭酒蕭衍、鎮西功曹謝朓、步兵校尉沈約、揚州秀才吳郡陸倕，並以文學，尤見親待，號曰八友。

translations.literal: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Le'an Ren Fang, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer of the Guards Army Xiao Yan, Merit Officer of the West Garrison Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and Yangzhou Presented Scholar Lu Chun of Wu Commandery—all famed for letters and especially favored—were called the Eight Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Ren Fang of Le'an, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer Xiao Yan, West Garrison merit officer Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and presented scholar Lu Chun of Wu—all celebrated for literature and especially cherished—were known as the Eight Friends.

sentences.zh: 法曹參軍柳惲、太學博士王僧孺、南徐州秀才濟陽江革、尚書殿中郎范縝、會稽孔休源亦預焉。

translations.literal: Legal Affairs Officer Liu Yun, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Sengru, South Xuzhou Presented Scholar Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun, Wang Sengru, Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji were among them as well.

sentences.zh: 琛，惠開之從子；

translations.literal: Chen was the son of a younger brother of Hui Kai;
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a nephew of Hui Kai;

sentences.zh: 惲，元景之從孫；

translations.literal: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;
translations.idiomatic: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;

sentences.zh: 融，僧達之孫；

translations.literal: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;
translations.idiomatic: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;

sentences.zh: 衍，順之之子；

translations.literal: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;

sentences.zh: 朓，述之孫；

translations.literal: Tiao was a grandson of Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Tiao was a grandson of Shu;

sentences.zh: 約，璞之子；

translations.literal: Yue was a son of Pu;
translations.idiomatic: Yue was a son of Pu;

sentences.zh: 僧孺，雅之曾孫；

translations.literal: Sengru was a great-grandson of Yazhi;
translations.idiomatic: Sengru was a great-grandson of Yazhi;

sentences.zh: 縝，雲之從兄也。

translations.literal: Zhen was Yun's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was Yun's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 子良篤好釋氏，招致名僧，講論佛法。

translations.literal: Ziliang was deeply devoted to the Buddha's teaching, invited famous monks, and lectured on Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was ardently devoted to Buddhism; he invited celebrated monks and held discussions on the dharma.

sentences.zh: 道俗之盛，江左未有。

translations.literal: Such splendor of clergy and laity, south of the Yangtze had never seen.
translations.idiomatic: The splendor of clergy and laity together had no precedent south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 或親為眾僧賦食、行水，世頗以為失宰相體。

translations.literal: Sometimes he personally apportioned food and carried water for the monks; the world largely thought this unbecoming of a chief minister's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: At times he personally served food and carried water for the monks—a conduct widely deemed unworthy of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 范縝盛稱無佛。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen loudly proclaimed that there is no Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen loudly maintained that there is no Buddha.

sentences.zh: 子良曰：「君不信因果，何得有富貴、貧賤？」

translations.literal: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how can there be wealth and honor, poverty and low estate?"
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in karma, how can there be rich and poor?"

sentences.zh: 縝曰：「人生如樹花同發，隨風而散：或拂簾幌墜茵席之上，或關籬牆落糞溷之中。

translations.literal: Zhen said, "Human life is like blossoms on a tree blooming together and scattering with the wind: some brush the curtain and fall on cushions and mats, some strike the fence and fall into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Human life is like flowers on a tree blooming at once and scattering in the wind—some brush the curtain and land on cushions, others hit the fence and fall into the dung pit.

sentences.zh: 墜茵席者，殿下是也；

translations.literal: Those who fall on cushions and mats—that is Your Highness;
translations.idiomatic: Those who land on cushions—that is you, my lord;

sentences.zh: 落糞溷者，下官是也。

translations.literal: those who fall into the privy—that is this humble official.
translations.idiomatic: those who fall into the dung pit—that is this humble official.

sentences.zh: 貴賤雖復殊途，因果竟在何處！」

translations.literal: Noble and base may take different paths, but where after all is cause and effect!"
translations.idiomatic: Noble and base may take different paths—where then is karma!"

sentences.zh: 子良無以難。

translations.literal: Ziliang had nothing with which to refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang had no answer.

sentences.zh: 縝又著《神滅論》，以為：「形者神之質，神者形之用也。

translations.literal: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," holding that "the body is the substance of the spirit; the spirit is the function of the body.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," arguing that "the body is the substance of the spirit, and the spirit is the function of the body.

sentences.zh: 神之於形，猶利之於刀；

translations.literal: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness in relation to a knife;
translations.idiomatic: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness to a blade;

sentences.zh: 未聞刀沒而利存，豈容形亡而神在哉！」

translations.literal: one has never heard of the knife perishing while sharpness remains—how could the body perish while the spirit endures!"
translations.idiomatic: no one has heard of the blade vanishing while sharpness remains—how then could the body perish while the spirit endures!"

sentences.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩，難之，終不能屈。

translations.literal: When this treatise appeared, court and countryside clamored; many challenged it, but in the end none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When the treatise appeared, court and country were in an uproar; critics assailed it, but none could refute him in the end.

sentences.zh: 太原王琰著論譏縝曰：「嗚呼范子！

translations.literal: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise to mock Zhen, saying, "Alas, Master Fan!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise mocking Zhen: "Alas, Master Fan!

sentences.zh: 曾不知其先祖神靈所在！」

translations.literal: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"
translations.idiomatic: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"

sentences.zh: 欲以杜縝後對。

translations.literal: He wished thereby to block Zhen from replying.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to silence any reply from Zhen.

sentences.zh: 縝對曰：「嗚呼王子！

translations.literal: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!

sentences.zh: 知其先祖神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之！」

translations.literal: You know where the spirits of your ancestors abide, yet cannot kill yourself to follow them!"
translations.idiomatic: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide, yet you cannot kill yourself to join them!"

sentences.zh: 子良使王融謂之曰：「以卿才美，何患不至中書郎；

translations.literal: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent and beauty, why worry that you will not reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent, why should you fail to reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 而故乖剌為此論，甚可惜也！

translations.literal: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how very regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how regrettable!

sentences.zh: 宜急毀棄之。」

translations.literal: You should hurry to destroy and abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: You should destroy it at once."

sentences.zh: 縝大笑曰：「使范縝賣論取官，已至令、僕矣，何但中書郎邪！」

translations.literal: Zhen laughed loudly and said, "If Fan Zhen were to sell his thesis for office, he would already have reached Minister and Vice Minister—why only Director of the Palace Secretariat!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen laughed and said, "If Fan Zhen sold his thesis for office, he would already be Minister or Vice Minister—why settle for mere Director of the Palace Secretariat!"

sentences.zh: 蕭衍好籌略，有文武才幹，王儉深器異之，曰：「蕭郎出三十，貴不可言。」

translations.literal: Xiao Yan loved strategy and had both civil and military talent; Wang Jian deeply valued and regarded him as extraordinary, saying, "When Master Xiao passes thirty, his eminence will be beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan was fond of strategy and possessed both civil and military gifts; Wang Jian held him in exceptional regard and said, "When Master Xiao passes thirty, his rank will be beyond telling."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以柳世隆為尚書左僕射，丹陽尹李安民為右僕射，王儉領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: On renyin, Liu Shilong was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Li Anmin of Danyang Intendant was made Right Vice Director, and Wang Jian acted as Danyang Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Liu Shilong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Danyang Intendant Li Anmin became Right Vice Director, and Wang Jian served concurrently as Danyang Intendant.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲寅，魏主如方山；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, the Wei ruler went to Mount Fang;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, the Northern Wei emperor went to Mount Fang;

sentences.zh: 戊午，還宮；

translations.literal: on wuwu, he returned to the palace;
translations.idiomatic: on wuwu he returned to the palace;

sentences.zh: 庚申，如鴻池；

translations.literal: on gengshen, he went to Hong Pool;
translations.idiomatic: on gengshen he went to Hong Pool;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，還宮。

translations.literal: on dingmao, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on dingmao he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲申，魏遣員外散騎常侍李彪等來聘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiashen, Wei sent Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Li Biao and others on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiashen, Northern Wei sent Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Li Biao and others on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬寅朔，中書舍人吳興茹法亮封望蔡男。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the renyin new moon, Palace Secretariat Attendant Ru Faliang of Wuxing was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the renyin new moon, Palace Secretariat Attendant Ru Faliang of Wuxing was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人四人，各住一省，謂之「四戶」，以法亮及臨海呂文顯等為之；

translations.literal: At that time there were four Palace Secretariat Attendants, each residing over one bureau—they were called the "Four Households"—and Faliang and Lü Wenxian of Linhai and others held these posts;
translations.idiomatic: At that time four Palace Secretariat Attendants each controlled one bureau and were known as the "Four Households"; Faliang, Lü Wenxian of Linhai, and others held these posts;

sentences.zh: 既總重權，勢傾朝廷，守宰數遷換去來，四方餉遺，歲數百萬。

translations.literal: having gathered heavy power, their influence tilted the court; prefects and magistrates were constantly transferred in and out, and gifts from the four quarters amounted to millions each year.
translations.idiomatic: once they held sweeping power their influence dominated the court; prefects and magistrates were constantly rotated, and gifts from every quarter totaled millions each year.

sentences.zh: 法亮嘗於眾中語人曰：「何需求外祿！

translations.literal: Faliang once said to people in a gathering, "Why seek extra salary!
translations.idiomatic: Faliang once said in public, "Why seek outside income!

sentences.zh: 此一戶中，年辦百萬。」

translations.literal: Within this one household, a million is handled each year."
translations.idiomatic: This one household alone brings in a million a year."

sentences.zh: 蓋約言之也。

translations.literal: This was roughly speaking.
translations.idiomatic: That was speaking in round terms.

sentences.zh: 後因天文有變，王儉極言「文顯等專權徇私，上天見異，禍由四戶」。

translations.literal: Later, because of celestial anomalies, Wang Jian spoke forcefully that "Wenxian and others monopolize power for private ends; Heaven shows anomalies—the calamity stems from the Four Households."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when celestial signs changed, Wang Jian argued forcefully that "Wenxian and the others abuse power for private gain; Heaven shows portents—the disaster comes from the Four Households."

sentences.zh: 上手詔酬答，而不能改也。

translations.literal: The emperor personally issued an edict in reply, yet could not change the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a personal edict in reply but could not change matters.

sentences.zh: 魏舊制：戶調帛二匹，絮二斤，絲一斤，谷二十斛；

translations.literal: Wei's old system: per household tax of two bolts of silk, two jin of floss, one jin of thread, and twenty hu of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Northern Wei system each household paid two bolts of silk, two jin of floss, one jin of thread, and twenty hu of grain;

sentences.zh: 又入帛一匹二丈，委之州庫，以供調外之費；

translations.literal: also one bolt and two zhang of silk paid in, deposited in the provincial treasury to supply extra-levy expenses;
translations.idiomatic: plus one bolt and two zhang of silk deposited in the provincial treasury for supplementary levies;

sentences.zh: 所調各隨土之所出。

translations.literal: what was levied in each case followed what the land produced.
translations.idiomatic: each levy followed local products.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔曰：「置官班祿，行之尚矣；

translations.literal: On dingmao, an edict said, "Establishing official ranks and salaries has long been practiced;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao an edict declared, "Establishing official ranks and salaries is an ancient practice;

sentences.zh: 自中原喪亂，茲制中絕。

translations.literal: since the Central Plains fell into chaos, this system was cut off midway.
translations.idiomatic: since the chaos in the Central Plains this system has lapsed.

sentences.zh: 朕憲章舊典，始班俸祿。

translations.literal: We take the old statutes as our model and now begin to distribute salaries.
translations.idiomatic: We now follow the ancient statutes and begin to distribute official salaries.

sentences.zh: 戶增調帛三匹，谷二斛九斗，以為官司之祿；

translations.literal: Per household the levy is increased by three bolts of silk and two hu nine dou of grain to serve as official salaries;
translations.idiomatic: Each household's levy is increased by three bolts of silk and two hu nine dou of grain to fund official salaries;

sentences.zh: 增調外帛二匹。

translations.literal: the extra-levy silk is increased by two bolts.
translations.idiomatic: the supplementary levy is increased by two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 祿行之後，贓滿一匹者死。

translations.literal: After salaries are instituted, anyone whose bribes reach one full bolt shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Once salaries are in place, anyone taking bribes of a full bolt or more shall be put to death.

sentences.zh: 變法改度，宜為更始，其大赦天下。」

translations.literal: To change laws and reform measures, a fresh beginning is fitting—let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: In changing laws and institutions a new beginning is fitting—let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲申，立皇子子倫為巴陵王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiashen, the prince Zilun was established as Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiashen, Prince Zilun was enfeoffed as Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏主如武州山石窟寺。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Wei ruler went to the cave temple at Mount Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the Northern Wei emperor visited the cave temple at Mount Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，魏詔，班祿以十月為始，季別受之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wei issued an edict: distribution of salaries begins in the tenth month and is received quarterly by season.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Northern Wei decreed that salary distribution would begin in the tenth month and be paid quarterly.

sentences.zh: 舊律，枉法十匹，義贓二十匹，罪死；

translations.literal: Under the old law, bending the law for ten bolts or taking improper gifts of twenty bolts was capital crime;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law, perverting justice for ten bolts or taking improper gifts of twenty bolts was punishable by death;

sentences.zh: 至是，義贓一匹，枉法無多少，皆死。

translations.literal: now improper gifts of one bolt, or bending the law regardless of amount—all were death.
translations.idiomatic: now one bolt of improper gift, or perverting justice in any amount—all were capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 仍分命使者，糾按守宰之貪者。

translations.literal: Envoys were also dispatched separately to investigate and prosecute greedy prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were also sent out to investigate corrupt prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 秦、益二州刺史恆農李洪之以外戚貴顯，為治貪暴，班祿之後，洪之首以贓敗。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhi of Hengnong, regional inspector of Qin and Yi provinces, was eminent as an affinal relative of the imperial house; his governance was greedy and violent—after salaries were instituted, Hongzhi was the first to fall for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhi of Hengnong, regional inspector of Qin and Yi, was eminent as an imperial affinal relative; his rule was greedy and brutal—after salaries were instituted he was the first official ruined by bribery.

sentences.zh: 魏主命鎖赴平城，集百官親臨數之；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered him shackled and brought to Pingcheng, gathered all officials, and personally enumerated his crimes;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him shackled and brought to Pingcheng, assembled the officials, and personally recounted his crimes;

sentences.zh: 猶以其大臣，聽在家自裁。

translations.literal: yet because he was a great minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.
translations.idiomatic: but because he was a senior minister he was allowed to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 自餘守宰坐贓死者四十餘人。

translations.literal: Besides him, more than forty prefects and magistrates were put to death for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty other prefects and magistrates were executed for bribery.

sentences.zh: 受祿者無不跼蹐，賕賂殆絕。

translations.literal: Those receiving salaries were all cramped and cautious; bribery nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Salary recipients were all on their guard; bribery nearly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 然吏民犯它罪者，魏主率寬之，疑罪奏讞多減死徙邊，歲以千計。

translations.literal: Yet for officials and commoners who committed other crimes, the Wei ruler was generally lenient; doubtful cases submitted for judgment were often commuted from death to exile on the frontier—thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for other offenses the emperor was generally lenient; doubtful cases were often commuted from death to frontier exile—thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 都下決大辟，歲不過五六人，州鎮亦簡。

translations.literal: In the capital, death sentences numbered no more than five or six a year; provinces and garrisons were likewise sparing.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital no more than five or six death sentences were handed down each year; provinces and garrisons were equally restrained.

sentences.zh: 久之，淮南王佗奏請依舊斷祿，文明太后召群臣議之。

translations.literal: After some time, Prince Huainan Tuo memorialized asking to abolish salaries as before; Empress Dowager Wenming summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Prince Huainan Tuo memorialized to abolish salaries as before; Empress Dowager Wenming convened the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 中書監高閭以為：「饑寒切身，慈母不能保其子。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lü held that "when hunger and cold press on the body, even a loving mother cannot protect her child.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lü argued, "When hunger and cold press close, even a loving mother cannot protect her child.

sentences.zh: 今給祿，則廉者足以無濫，貪者足以勸慕；

translations.literal: Now if salaries are given, the honest will have enough not to overreach, and the greedy will have enough to be encouraged toward emulation;
translations.idiomatic: With salaries in place the honest have enough to refrain from excess, and the greedy have enough to be drawn toward integrity;

sentences.zh: 不給，則貪者得肆其奸，廉者不能自保。

translations.literal: if not given, the greedy can unleash their wickedness and the honest cannot protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: without them the greedy can indulge their schemes and the honest cannot protect themselves.

sentences.zh: 淮南之議，不亦謬乎！」

translations.literal: Is not Prince Huainan's proposal utterly mistaken!"
translations.idiomatic: Is not Prince Huainan's proposal utterly mistaken!"

sentences.zh: 詔從閭議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Lü's view.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted Lü's position.

sentences.zh: 閭又上表，以為：「北狄悍愚，同於禽獸。

translations.literal: Lü also submitted a memorial, holding that "the northern Di are fierce and stupid, the same as birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Lü also submitted a memorial arguing that "the northern barbarians are fierce and dull-witted, no better than birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 所長者野戰，所短者攻城。

translations.literal: What they excel at is field battle; what they are poor at is storming cities.
translations.idiomatic: They excel at field battle and are weak at siege warfare.

sentences.zh: 若以狄之所短奪其所長，則雖眾不能成患，雖來不能深入。

translations.literal: If we use what the Di are poor at to overcome what they excel at, then though numerous they cannot become a calamity, and though they come they cannot penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: If we use their weaknesses against their strengths, then even in great numbers they cannot become a threat, and even when they come they cannot penetrate deeply.

sentences.zh: 又，狄散居野澤，隨逐水草，戰則與家業並至，奔則與畜牧俱逃，不繼資糧而飲食自足，是以歷代能為邊患。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Di scatter and dwell in wild marshes, following water and grass; when they fight, household goods come with them, when they flee, livestock flees with them—they need no continuing supplies of grain and provisions yet food and drink are self-sufficient; therefore through the ages they have been able to become frontier troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they live scattered in wild marshes, following pasture and water; in battle their households come with them, in flight their herds flee with them—they need no supply trains yet food and drink are always at hand; thus through the ages they have plagued the frontier.

sentences.zh: 六鎮勢分，倍眾不鬥，互相圍逼，難以制之。

translations.literal: The Six Garrisons' forces are divided; with twice the numbers they will not fight; they surround and press one another—hard to control them.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Garrisons' forces are divided; even with twice the enemy's numbers they will not engage; they hem one another in and are hard to control.

sentences.zh: 請依秦、漢故事，於六鎮之北築長城，擇要害之地，往往開門，造小城於其側，置兵扞守。

translations.literal: I ask that following Qin and Han precedent a long wall be built north of the Six Garrisons, choosing strategic places, opening gates here and there, building small cities at their sides, and stationing troops to defend.
translations.idiomatic: I propose following Qin and Han precedent to build a long wall north of the Six Garrisons, choosing strategic points, opening gates at intervals, erecting small fortresses beside them, and garrisoning troops to hold them.

sentences.zh: 狄既不攻城，野掠無獲，草盡則走，終必懲艾。

translations.literal: Since the Di do not storm cities, wild raiding gains nothing; when grass is exhausted they depart—in the end they will surely be chastened.
translations.idiomatic: Since they do not storm cities, raiding will yield nothing; when pasture is exhausted they will withdraw—in time they will surely be subdued.

sentences.zh: 計六鎮東西不過千里，一夫一月之功，可城三步之地，強弱相兼，不過用十萬人，一月可就；

translations.literal: Calculating that east to west of the Six Garrisons is no more than a thousand li, one man's labor in one month can wall three paces of ground; combining strong and weak, no more than a hundred thousand men are needed—it can be finished in one month;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Garrisons span no more than a thousand li east to west; one man's month of labor walls three paces; combining strong and weak labor, no more than a hundred thousand men are needed and the work can be finished in a month;

sentences.zh: 雖有暫勞，可以永逸。

translations.literal: though there is temporary toil, perpetual ease can be gained.
translations.idiomatic: though the labor is temporary, the peace will be lasting.

sentences.zh: 凡長城有五利：罷游防之苦，一也；

translations.literal: In all the long wall has five benefits: ending the hardship of roaming defense—first;
translations.idiomatic: The long wall offers five benefits: ending the hardship of roaming patrols—first;

sentences.zh: 北部放牧無抄掠之患，二也；

translations.literal: northern pastures for grazing without the trouble of raids—second;
translations.idiomatic: northern pastures free from raiding—second;

sentences.zh: 登城觀敵，以逸待勞，三也；

translations.literal: ascending the walls to watch the enemy and awaiting them at ease—third;
translations.idiomatic: watching the enemy from the walls and meeting them refreshed—third;

sentences.zh: 息無時之備，四也；

translations.literal: ending the burden of constant readiness—fourth;
translations.idiomatic: ending the burden of perpetual alert—fourth;

sentences.zh: 歲常游運，永得不匱，五也。」

translations.literal: grain transported annually by water, never exhausted—fifth."
translations.idiomatic: annual transport by water, never wanting—fifth."

sentences.zh: 魏主優詔答之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor responded with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁巳，以南徐州刺史長沙王晃為中書監。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, Prince of Changsha Huang, regional inspector of South Xuzhou, was made Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, Prince of Changsha Huang, regional inspector of South Xuzhou, was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖臨終，以晃屬帝，使處於輦下或近籓，勿令遠出。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founder was dying, he entrusted Huang to the emperor, directing that he remain near the capital or a nearby fief and not be sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on his deathbed the Founder entrusted Huang to the emperor, ordering that he stay near the capital or a nearby fief and not be sent far away.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「宋氏若非骨肉相殘，它族豈得乘其弊！

translations.literal: He also said, "If the Song house had not torn itself apart in fratricide, how could another clan have seized its weakness!
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Had the Song not destroyed one another, how could another house have exploited their weakness!

sentences.zh: 汝深誡之！」

translations.literal: You must take this deeply to heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Take this deeply to heart!"

sentences.zh: 舊制：諸王在都，唯得置捉刀左右四十人。

translations.literal: Under the old rule, princes in the capital might keep only forty armed attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule princes in the capital might keep only forty armed attendants.

sentences.zh: 晃好武飾，及罷南徐州，私載數百人仗還建康，為禁司所覺，投之江水。

translations.literal: Huang loved martial display; when he left South Xuzhou he secretly brought back several hundred men's weapons to Jiankang, was discovered by the prohibition office, and they were thrown into the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Huang loved martial display; when he left South Xuzhou he secretly brought hundreds of weapons back to Jiankang; the prohibition office discovered them and they were thrown into the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大怒，將糾以法，豫章王嶷叩頭流涕曰：「晃罪誠不足宥；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was furious and was about to punish him by law; Prince of Yuzhang Liao kowtowed with tears, saying, "Huang's crime truly does not deserve pardon;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard he was furious and was about to punish Huang by law; Prince of Yuzhang Liao kowtowed in tears and said, "Huang's crime truly deserves no pardon;

sentences.zh: 陛下當憶先朝念晃。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should remember how the former court cherished Huang."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should remember how the former emperor cherished Huang."

sentences.zh: 帝亦垂泣，由是終無異意，然亦不被親寵。

translations.literal: The emperor also wept; from this he never again harbored ill will, yet Huang was never warmly favored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well; from then on he never again harbored ill will toward Huang, yet Huang was never warmly favored.

sentences.zh: 論者謂帝優於魏文，減於漢明。

translations.literal: Commentators said the emperor surpassed Emperor Wen of Wei but fell short of Emperor Ming of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that the emperor surpassed Cao Pi of Wei but fell short of Emperor Ming of Han.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄多才藝而疏心幸，亦無寵於帝。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Ye was talented in many arts but careless in winning favor and likewise was not favored by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuling Ye was gifted in many arts but careless about winning favor and was likewise not favored by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，醉伏地，貂抄肉拌。

translations.literal: Once while attending a banquet he was drunk and lay face down; his sable collar was smeared with meat.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet he was drunk and collapsed face down; his sable collar was smeared with meat.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「肉污貂。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "The meat has soiled the sable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "The meat has soiled the sable."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下愛羽毛而疏骨肉。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty cherishes feathers but neglects flesh and bone."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty cherishes fur but neglects kin."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 曄輕財好施，故無畜積；

translations.literal: Ye was light with wealth and fond of giving, so he had no savings;
translations.idiomatic: Ye was generous with money and fond of giving, so he had no savings;

sentences.zh: 名後堂山曰「首陽」，蓋怨貧薄也。

translations.literal: he named the hill behind his hall "Shouyang," expressing resentment at his poverty.
translations.idiomatic: he named the hill behind his hall "Shouyang," voicing resentment at his poverty.

sentences.zh: 高麗王璉遣使入貢於魏，亦入貢於齊。

translations.literal: King Rian of Goguryeo sent envoys to offer tribute to Wei and also to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: King Rian of Goguryeo sent envoys to offer tribute to Northern Wei and also to Qi.

sentences.zh: 時高麗方強，魏置諸國使邸，齊使第一，高麗次之。

translations.literal: At that time Goguryeo was strong; Wei established lodging for envoys of various states—Qi envoys ranked first, Goguryeo second.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo was then powerful; Northern Wei established lodging for foreign envoys—Qi envoys ranked first, Goguryeo second.

sentences.zh: 益州大度獠恃險驕恣，前後刺史不能制。

translations.literal: The Dadu Liao of Yizhou relied on rugged terrain and were arrogant and unrestrained; successive regional inspectors could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadu Liao of Yizhou relied on rugged terrain and were arrogant and unruly; successive regional inspectors could not control them.

sentences.zh: 及陳顯達為刺史，遣使責其租賧。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda became regional inspector, he sent envoys to demand their tribute levies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda became regional inspector, he sent envoys to demand their tribute levies.

sentences.zh: 獠帥曰：「兩眼刺史尚不敢調我，況一眼乎！」

translations.literal: The Liao chief said, "A two-eyed regional inspector still did not dare press me—how much less a one-eyed man!"
translations.idiomatic: The Liao chief said, "A two-eyed regional inspector did not dare press me—how much less a one-eyed man!"

sentences.zh: 遂殺其使。

translations.literal: He then killed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed the envoy.

sentences.zh: 顯達分部將吏，聲言出獵，夜往襲之，男女無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Xianda divided his officers and clerks, announced he was going hunting, attacked by night, and beheaded men and women of every age.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda divided his officers, announced a hunting expedition, attacked by night, and beheaded men and women of every age.

sentences.zh: 晉氏以來，益州刺史皆以名將為之。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house, regional inspectors of Yizhou have always been famous generals.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin dynasty, regional inspectors of Yizhou had always been famous generals.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，帝始以始興王鑒為督益、寧諸軍事、益州刺史，征顯達為中護軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, the emperor for the first time made Prince of Shixing Jian Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yi and Ning and regional inspector of Yizhou, and summoned Xianda to be Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, the emperor for the first time made Prince of Shixing Jian supervisor of military affairs for Yi and Ning and regional inspector of Yizhou, and summoned Xianda to serve as Central Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 先是，劫帥韓武方聚黨千餘人斷流為暴，郡縣不能禁。

translations.literal: Earlier, the bandit chief Han Wufang had gathered a party of more than a thousand men, blocked the river, and committed violence; commanderies and counties could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the bandit chief Han Wufang had gathered more than a thousand followers, blocked the river, and committed violence; commanderies and counties could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 鑒行至上明，武方出降，長史虞悰等鹹請殺之。

translations.literal: When Jian's procession reached Shangming, Wufang came out to surrender; Chief Clerk Yu Cong and others all asked that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian reached Shangming, Wufang came out to surrender; Chief Clerk Yu Cong and others all urged that he be killed.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「殺之失信，且無以勸善。」

translations.literal: Jian said, "To kill him would break faith and offer no way to encourage goodness."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "To kill him would break faith and offer no way to encourage goodness."

sentences.zh: 乃啟台而宥之，於是巴西蠻夷為寇暴者皆望風降附。

translations.literal: He then reported to the capital and pardoned him; thereupon all the barbarian raiders of Baxi who had committed violence submitted at the news.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the capital and pardoned him; thereafter all the barbarian raiders of Baxi submitted at the news.

sentences.zh: 鑒時年十四，行至新城，道路籍籍，云「陳顯達大選士馬，不肯就征。」

translations.literal: Jian was then fourteen; when his procession reached Xincheng, rumor spread along the road that "Chen Xianda is greatly selecting soldiers and horses and refuses to accept the summons."
translations.idiomatic: Jian was only fourteen; when he reached Xincheng, rumor spread that "Chen Xianda is mustering troops and refuses to accept the summons."

sentences.zh: 乃停新城，遣典簽張曇皙往觀形勢。

translations.literal: He therefore halted at Xincheng and sent Registrar Zhang Tanxi to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Xincheng and sent Registrar Zhang Tanxi to observe the situation.

sentences.zh: 俄而顯達遣使詣鑒，鹹勸鑒執之。

translations.literal: Soon Xianda sent envoys to Jian; all urged Jian to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianda sent envoys to Jian; all urged Jian to seize them.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「顯達立節本朝，必自無此。」

translations.literal: Jian said, "Xianda has established his integrity toward this court—he surely would not do this himself."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Xianda has proven his loyalty to this court—he would never do such a thing."

sentences.zh: 居二日，曇皙還，具言「顯達已遷家出城，日夕望殿下至。」

translations.literal: After two days Tanxi returned and reported in full that "Xianda has already moved his household out of the city and awaits Your Highness day and night."
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Tanxi returned and reported that "Xianda has already moved his household out of the city and awaits Your Highness day and night."

sentences.zh: 於是乃前。

translations.literal: Only then did he advance.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he advance.

sentences.zh: 鑒喜文學，器服如素士，蜀人悅之。

translations.literal: Jian loved letters; his vessels and dress were like those of a plain scholar—the people of Shu were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian loved literature; his dress and furnishings were like those of a plain scholar—the people of Shu were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏員外散騎常侍李彪等來聘。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Wei Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Li Biao and others came on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Northern Wei Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Li Biao and others came on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔增豫章王嶷封邑為四千戶。

translations.literal: That year, an edict increased Prince of Yuzhang Liao's fief to four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict increased Prince of Yuzhang Liao's fief to four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉之世，諸王入齋閣，得白服、裙帽見人主；

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, when princes entered the fasting hall they might wear white robes and skirted caps to see the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, when princes entered the fasting hall they might wear white robes and skirted caps to see the sovereign;

sentences.zh: 唯出太極四廟，乃備朝服。

translations.literal: only when leaving the four temples of the Supreme Ultimate did they don full court dress.
translations.idiomatic: only when leaving the four temples of the Supreme Ultimate did they don full court dress.

sentences.zh: 自後此制遂絕。

translations.literal: Afterward this rule was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward this custom lapsed.

sentences.zh: 上於嶷友愛，宮中曲宴，聽依元嘉故事。

translations.literal: The emperor was affectionate toward Liao; at private palace banquets he permitted the Yuanjia precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was affectionate toward Liao; at private palace banquets he permitted the Yuanjia precedent.

sentences.zh: 嶷固辭不敢，唯車駕至其第，乃白服、烏紗帽以侍宴。

translations.literal: Liao firmly declined and did not dare; only when the imperial carriage came to his residence did he wear white robes and a black gauze cap to attend the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Liao firmly declined; only when the imperial carriage came to his residence did he wear white robes and a black gauze cap to attend the banquet.

sentences.zh: 至於衣服、器服制度，動皆陳啟，事無專制，務從減省。

translations.literal: As for regulations on clothing and vessels, he always reported them for approval; nothing was decided on his own authority, and he strove for reduction and economy.
translations.idiomatic: As for regulations on clothing and vessels, he always reported them for approval; nothing was decided on his own authority, and he strove for economy.

sentences.zh: 上並不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not permit any of it.

sentences.zh: 嶷常慮盛滿，求解揚州，以授竟陵王子良。

translations.literal: Liao often feared reaching the height of fullness and asked to be relieved of Yangzhou to give it to Prince Jingling of Jingling, Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Liao often feared the dangers of excess and asked to be relieved of Yangzhou to give it to Prince Jingling Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 上終不許，曰：「畢汝一世，無所多言。」

translations.literal: The emperor would not permit it, saying, "For your whole lifetime, say no more of it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not permit it, saying, "For your whole lifetime, say no more of it."

sentences.zh: 嶷長七尺八寸，善修容範，文物衛從，禮冠百僚，每出入殿省，瞻望者無不肅然。

translations.literal: Liao was seven chi eight cun tall, skilled at cultivating his appearance; his ceremonial regalia and escort outshone all officials—each time he entered or left the palace halls, those who looked on were without exception awed.
translations.idiomatic: Liao stood seven chi eight cun tall and cultivated his bearing with care; his ceremonial regalia and escort outshone all officials—each time he entered or left the palace halls, onlookers were awed.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史李叔獻既受命，而斷割外國貢獻；

translations.literal: Li Shuxian of Jiaozhou, having received his appointment, cut off foreign tribute;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuxian of Jiaozhou, having received his appointment, cut off foreign tribute;

sentences.zh: 上欲討之。

translations.literal: the emperor wished to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor wished to punish him.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 3 (

sentences.zh: 乙丑，公元四八五年）

translations.literal: yichou, the year 485 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yichou, corresponding to 485 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙辰，以大司農劉楷為交州刺史，發南康、廬陵、始興兵以討叔獻。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu Kai was made regional inspector of Jiaozhou; troops from Nankang, Luling, and Shixing were raised to attack Shuxian.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu Kai was appointed regional inspector of Jiaozhou; troops from Nankang, Luling, and Shixing were raised to attack Shuxian.

sentences.zh: 叔獻耳之，遣使乞更申數年，獻十二隊純銀兜鍪及孔雀毦；

translations.literal: Shuxian heard of it and sent envoys begging a few more years' grace, offering twelve sets of pure-silver helmets and peacock-feather canopies;
translations.idiomatic: Shuxian heard of it and sent envoys begging a few more years' grace, offering twelve sets of pure-silver helmets and peacock-feather canopies;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 叔獻懼為楷所襲，間道自湘川還朝。

translations.literal: Shuxian, fearing an attack by Kai, returned to court by a hidden route through the Xiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxian, fearing an attack by Kai, returned to court by a hidden route through the Xiang River.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏詔曰：「圖讖之興，出於三季，既非經國之典，徒為妖邪所憑。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Wei issued an edict: "The rise of prognostic charts comes from the three degenerate ages; they are not classics for governing the state but merely rely on demonic evil.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Northern Wei issued an edict: "Prognostic charts arose in the three degenerate ages; they are not classics of statecraft but merely tools of demonic evil.

sentences.zh: 自今圖讖、秘緯，一皆焚之，留者以大辟論！」

translations.literal: From now on all prognostic charts and secret weft-texts are to be burned; whoever keeps them shall be judged by the great penalty of death!"
translations.idiomatic: From now on all prognostic charts and secret weft-texts are to be burned; whoever keeps them shall be put to death!"

sentences.zh: 又嚴禁諸巫覡及委巷卜筮非經典所載者。

translations.literal: Diviners and shamans were also strictly forbidden, as were back-alley divinations not recorded in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners and shamans were also strictly forbidden, as were back-alley divinations not recorded in the classics.

sentences.zh: 魏馮太后作《皇誥》十八篇，癸未，大饗群臣於太華殿，班《皇誥》。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng of Wei composed eighteen chapters of "Imperial Admonitions"; on guiwei she gave a great feast to the ministers in the Hall of Supreme Splendor and distributed the "Imperial Admonitions."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng of Northern Wei composed eighteen chapters of "Imperial Admonitions"; on guiwei she gave a great feast to the ministers in the Hall of Supreme Splendor and distributed the "Imperial Admonitions."

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 詔復立國學；

translations.literal: An edict restored the National University;
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the National University;

sentences.zh: 釋奠先師用上公禮。

translations.literal: the ceremony of offering to the former teacher used the rites of a senior duke.
translations.idiomatic: the ceremony honoring the former teacher used the rites of a senior duke.

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，魏制皇子皇孫有封爵者，歲祿各有差。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jihai, Wei regulated that imperial sons and grandsons with enfeoffed ranks should receive annual stipends in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, Northern Wei regulated that imperial sons and grandsons with enfeoffed ranks should receive annual stipends in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上祭北郊。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the emperor sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙申，魏封皇弟禧為咸陽王，干為河南王，羽為廣陵王，雍為穎川王，勰為始平王，詳為北海王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingshen, Wei enfeoffed the emperor's younger brother Xi as Prince of Xianyang, Gan as Prince of Henan, Yu as Prince of Guangling, Yong as Prince of Yingchuan, Xie as Prince of Shiping, and Xiang as Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, Northern Wei enfeoffed the emperor's younger brother Xi as Prince of Xianyang, Gan as Prince of Henan, Yu as Prince of Guangling, Yong as Prince of Yingchuan, Xie as Prince of Shiping, and Xiang as Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 文明太后令置學館，選師傅以教諸王。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered academies established and teachers chosen to instruct the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered academies established and teachers chosen to instruct the princes.

sentences.zh: 勰于兄弟最賢，敏而好學，善屬文，魏主尤奇愛之。

translations.literal: Among the brothers Xie was the most worthy—quick and fond of learning, skilled at composition; the Wei ruler especially cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the brothers Xie was the most worthy—quick-witted and fond of learning, skilled at composition; the Northern Wei emperor especially cherished him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸丑，魏主如方山；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, the Wei ruler went to Mount Fang;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, the Northern Wei emperor went to Mount Fang;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，還宮。

translations.literal: on jiayin, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jiayin he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 初，宋太宗置總明觀以集學士，亦謂之東觀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Taizong of Song established the Zongming Observatory to gather scholars—it was also called the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong of Liu Song established the Zongming Observatory to gather scholars—it was also called the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 上以國學既立，五月，乙未，省總明觀。

translations.literal: Since the National University had been established, in the fifth month, on yiwei, the emperor abolished the Zongming Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Since the National University had been established, in the fifth month, on yiwei, the emperor abolished the Zongming Observatory.

sentences.zh: 時王儉領國子祭酒，詔於儉宅開學士館，以總明四部書充之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jian was acting as Libationer of the National University; an edict opened a scholars' hall at Jian's residence and filled it with the four divisions of books from Zongming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was then acting as Libationer of the National University; an edict opened a scholars' hall at Jian's residence and stocked it with the four divisions of books from Zongming.

sentences.zh: 又詔儉以家為府。

translations.literal: An edict also made Jian's home his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also made Jian's home his official residence.

sentences.zh: 自宋世祖好文章，士大夫悉以文章相尚，無以專經為業者。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Shizu of Song loved belles-lettres, the scholar-officials all esteemed literary composition and none made the classics their sole profession.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Shizu of Liu Song loved belles-lettres, scholar-officials all esteemed literary composition and none made the classics their sole profession.

sentences.zh: 儉少好《禮》學及《春秋》，言論造次必於儒者，由是衣冠翕然，更尚儒術。

translations.literal: Jian from youth loved the study of the Rites and the Spring and Autumn Annals; in speech he always followed the Confucians—thereby the gentry converged and came again to esteem Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Jian from youth loved the Rites and the Spring and Autumn Annals; in speech he always followed the Confucians—thereby the gentry converged and came again to esteem Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 儉撰次朝儀、國典，自晉、宋以來故事，無不諳憶，故當朝理事，斷決如流。

translations.literal: Jian compiled court ritual and state statutes; precedents from Jin and Song onward he knew by heart—therefore in governing the court his decisions flowed like water.
translations.idiomatic: Jian compiled court ritual and state statutes; precedents from Jin and Song onward he knew by heart—therefore in governing the court his decisions flowed effortlessly.

sentences.zh: 每博議引證，八坐、丞、郎無能異者。

translations.literal: Whenever broad deliberation cited precedent, none among the eight ministers, assistants, or directors could dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever broad deliberation cited precedent, none among the eight ministers, assistants, or directors could dissent.

sentences.zh: 令史咨事常數十人，賓客滿席，儉應接辨析，傍無留滯，發言下筆，皆有音彩。

translations.literal: When clerks consulted on affairs there were often dozens at once; guests filled the seats—Jian answered and analyzed without delay at his side; whether speaking or writing, all had literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks consulted on affairs there were often dozens at once; guests filled the seats—Jian answered and analyzed without delay; whether speaking or writing, all had literary grace.

sentences.zh: 十日一還學監試諸生，巾卷在庭，劍衛、令史，儀容甚盛。

translations.literal: Every ten days he returned to the academy to supervise examinations of the students; scholars' scrolls filled the courtyard, sword guards and clerks—the spectacle was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days he returned to the academy to supervise student examinations; scholars' scrolls filled the courtyard, sword guards and clerks—the spectacle was very grand.

sentences.zh: 作解散髻，斜插簪，朝野慕之，相與倣傚。

translations.literal: He wore a loose coiffure with pins inserted at a slant—court and country admired it and imitated one another.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a loose coiffure with pins inserted at a slant—court and country admired it and imitated him.

sentences.zh: 儉常謂人曰：「江左風流宰相，唯有謝安。」

translations.literal: Jian often told people, "Among the elegant chief ministers of the lands south of the Yangtze, only Xie An."
translations.idiomatic: Jian often said, "Among the elegant chief ministers south of the Yangtze, only Xie An."

sentences.zh: 意以自比也。

translations.literal: He meant to compare himself.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to compare himself.

sentences.zh: 上深委仗之，士流選用，奏無不可。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply relied on him; for selecting men of the gentry, no memorial was ever denied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply relied on him; for selecting men of the gentry, no memorial was ever denied.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚戌，魏進河南王度易侯為車騎將軍，遣給事中吳興丘冠先使河南，並送柔然使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengxu, Wei promoted Prince of Henan, Chief Tuyuhun, to General of Chariots and Cavalry and sent Palace Attendant Qiu Guanxian of Wuxing as envoy to Henan, also escorting a Rouran envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengxu, Northern Wei promoted the Prince of Henan, Chief Tuyuhun, to General of Chariots and Cavalry and sent Palace Attendant Qiu Guanxian of Wuxing as envoy to Henan, also escorting a Rouran envoy.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏主如方山。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Wei ruler went to Mount Fang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Northern Wei emperor went to Mount Fang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On dingsi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，魏遣使拜宕昌王梁彌機兄子彌承為宕昌王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, Wei sent envoys to invest Liang Miji's elder brother's son Micheng as King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, Northern Wei sent envoys to invest Micheng, nephew of King Dangchang Liang Miji, as King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 初，彌機死，子彌博立，為吐谷渾所逼，奔仇池。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Miji died, his son Mibo succeeded but was pressed by Tuyuhun and fled to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Miji died, his son Mibo succeeded but was pressed by Tuyuhun and fled to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 仇池鎮將穆亮以彌機事魏素厚，矜其滅亡；

translations.literal: Mu Liang, garrison commander of Chouchi, because Miji had long been devoted to Wei, pitied the family's destruction;
translations.idiomatic: Mu Liang, garrison commander of Chouchi, because Miji had long been devoted to Northern Wei, pitied the family's destruction;

sentences.zh: 彌博凶悖，所部惡之；

translations.literal: Mibo was fierce and perverse and his followers hated him;
translations.idiomatic: Mibo was fierce and perverse and his followers hated him;

sentences.zh: 彌承為眾所附，表請納之。

translations.literal: Micheng was attached to by the multitude; he memorialized asking to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Micheng was supported by the people; he memorialized asking to receive him.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 亮帥騎三萬軍於龍鵠，擊走吐谷渾，立彌承而還。

translations.literal: Liang led thirty thousand cavalry to Longhu, routed Tuyuhun, established Micheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liang led thirty thousand cavalry to Longhu, routed Tuyuhun, established Micheng, and returned.

sentences.zh: 亮，崇之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Liang was a great-grandson of Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a great-grandson of Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏主如魚池，登青原岡；

translations.literal: On wuzi, the Wei ruler went to Fish Pool and ascended Green Plain Mound;
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Northern Wei emperor went to Fish Pool and climbed Green Plain Mound;

sentences.zh: 甲午，還宮；

translations.literal: On jiawu, he returned to the palace;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he returned to the palace;

sentences.zh: 八月，己亥，如彌澤；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jihai, he went to Mize;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jihai, he went to Mize;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，登牛頭山；

translations.literal: On jiayin, he ascended Ox Head Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he climbed Ox Head Mountain;

sentences.zh: 甲子，還宮。

translations.literal: On jiazi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魏初，民多廕附；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, the people widely sought yinfu patronage;
translations.idiomatic: In the early Northern Wei, many commoners attached themselves to powerful patrons for protection;

sentences.zh: 廕附者皆無官役，而豪強征斂倍於公賦。

translations.literal: Those under yinfu owed no official corvée, yet the powerful exacted levies double the public tax.
translations.idiomatic: Such dependents owed no state corvée, yet local magnates extracted from them twice what the public tax demanded.

sentences.zh: 給事中李安世上言：「歲饑民流，田業多為豪右所佔奪；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Anshi memorialized: "In years of famine the people drift away, and fields are largely seized by the powerful;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Li Anshi submitted a memorial: "In famine years the people flee, and much farmland is seized by powerful families;

sentences.zh: 雖桑井難復，宜更均量，使力業相稱。

translations.literal: though mulberry groves and wells are hard to restore, land should be re-measured and equalized so that labor and holdings match.
translations.idiomatic: although old homesteads cannot always be restored, land should be remeasured and reallocated so that each household's labor matches its holding.

sentences.zh: 又，所爭之田，宜限年斷，事久難明，悉歸今主，以絕詐妄。」

translations.literal: Moreover, disputed fields should be cut off by a time limit; when long-standing cases cannot be clarified, all should go to the present holder, to end fraud and false claims."
translations.idiomatic: Disputed fields, too, should be settled by a statute of limitations: when old claims can no longer be proved, ownership should pass to the current holder, cutting off fraud and false litigation."

sentences.zh: 魏主善之，由是始議均田。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler approved this, and from this began discussion of equal-field distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor approved the proposal, and from this the equal-field system first came under discussion.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁未，詔遣使者循行州郡，與牧守均給天下之田：諸男夫十五以上受露田四十畝，婦人二十畝，奴婢依良丁；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei, an edict sent envoys to tour the provinces and commanderies and, with governors and prefects, equally distribute the empire's fields: every adult male fifteen and above received forty mu of open-field land, women twenty mu, and slaves and maidservants according to free adult males;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei, an edict dispatched envoys to tour the provinces and commanderies and, together with local governors and prefects, equally distribute land throughout the realm: every adult male aged fifteen or above was to receive forty mu of open-field land, women twenty mu, and slaves and maidservants on the same basis as free adult males;

sentences.zh: 牛一頭，受田三十畝，限止四牛。

translations.literal: one ox received thirty mu of land, with a limit of four oxen.
translations.idiomatic: each ox received thirty mu of land, up to a maximum of four oxen.

sentences.zh: 所授之田，率倍之；

translations.literal: The land granted was as a rule doubled;
translations.idiomatic: The land actually granted was, as a rule, doubled;

sentences.zh: 三易之田，再倍之，以供耕作及還受之盈縮。

translations.literal: fields requiring three rotations were doubled again, to supply cultivation and the surplus or shortfall in grants and returns.
translations.idiomatic: fields requiring three crop rotations were doubled again, to cover cultivation needs and the surplus or shortfall when land was granted and returned.

sentences.zh: 人年及課則受田，老免及身沒則還田。

translations.literal: When a person reached taxable age he received land; when exempted by old age or upon death, the land was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When a person reached taxable age he received land; when he was exempted by old age or upon his death, the land was returned.

sentences.zh: 奴婢、牛隨有無以還受。

translations.literal: Slaves, maidservants, and oxen were returned or granted according to whether they were present or absent.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves, maidservants, and oxen were granted or returned according to whether the household still had them.

sentences.zh: 初受田者，男夫給二十畝，課種桑五十株；

translations.literal: Those receiving land for the first time were given twenty mu to adult males, with a levy of fifty mulberry trees to be planted;
translations.idiomatic: First-time recipients were allotted twenty mu of mulberry land for each adult male, with a requirement to plant fifty mulberry trees;

sentences.zh: 桑田皆為世業，身終不還。

translations.literal: mulberry land all became hereditary property and was never returned during one's lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: mulberry land became permanent hereditary property and was never returned during the holder's lifetime.

sentences.zh: 恆計見口，有盈者無受無還，不足者受種如法，盈者得賣其盈。

translations.literal: Households were constantly reckoned by present mouths: where there was surplus, no grant and no return; where there was shortfall, grants were made according to law; those with surplus might sell the excess.
translations.idiomatic: Households were continually assessed by the number of persons actually present: surplus members received no land and required no return; shortfalls were filled according to law; and households with excess land could sell the surplus.

sentences.zh: 諸宰民之官，各隨近給公田有差，更代相付；

translations.literal: All officials who governed the people were given official fields nearby in graded amounts, transferred from one term to the next;
translations.idiomatic: All officials charged with governing the people were allotted nearby official fields in graded amounts, to be transferred from one term of office to the next;

sentences.zh: 賣者坐如律。

translations.literal: those who sold illegally were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who sold such land illegally was punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏魏郡王陳建卒。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Wei Prince of Wei Commandery Chen Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Chen Jian, Prince of Wei Commandery in Northern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 魏員外散騎常侍李彪等來聘。

translations.literal: Wei Supernumerary Palace Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry Li Biao and others came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao, Supernumerary Palace Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry of Northern Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，魏以侍中淮南王佗為司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Wei appointed Palace Attendant Prince of Huainan Tuo as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Northern Wei appointed Palace Attendant Prince of Huainan, Tuo, as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 柔然犯魏塞，魏任城王澄帥眾拒之，柔然遁去。

translations.literal: Rouran violated Wei's frontier defenses; Wei Prince of Rencheng Cheng led troops to repel them, and Rouran fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran raided the Northern Wei frontier; Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng led troops to repel them, and the Rouran withdrew.

sentences.zh: 澄，雲之子也。

translations.literal: Cheng was the son of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was the son of Yun.

sentences.zh: 氐、羌反，詔以澄為都督梁、益、荊三州諸軍事、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang rebelled, and an edict made Cheng Grand Commander over all military affairs of Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces and Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di and Qiang rebelled, an edict appointed Cheng Grand Commander over all military affairs of Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces and Inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 澄至州，討叛柔服，氐、羌皆平。

translations.literal: When Cheng reached the province, he punished rebels and soothed the compliant, and the Di and Qiang were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng reached the province, he punished rebels and won over the compliant, and both the Di and Qiang were pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖命黃門郎虞玩之等檢定黃籍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Founding Emperor had ordered Yellow Gate Gentleman Yu Wanzhi and others to examine and fix the yellow registers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Founding Emperor had ordered Yellow Gate Gentleman Yu Wanzhi and others to examine and rectify the yellow household registers.

sentences.zh: 上即位，別立校籍官，置令史，限人一日得數巧。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he separately established registry-verification offices, appointed clerks, and required each person to uncover several fraudulent cases in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, he separately established registry-verification offices, appointed clerks, and required each clerk to uncover several fraudulent cases in a single day.

sentences.zh: 既連年不已，民愁怨不安。

translations.literal: This continued year after year without end, and the people grew anxious, resentful, and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The verification went on year after year without end, and the people grew anxious, resentful, and unsettled.

sentences.zh: 外監會稽呂文度啟上，籍被卻者悉充遠戍，民多逃亡避罪。

translations.literal: Outer Supervisor Lü Wendu of Kuaiji reported to the emperor that all whose registers were rejected were sent to distant frontier garrison duty, and many people fled to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Supervisor Lü Wendu of Kuaiji reported to the emperor that everyone whose registry entry was rejected was sent to distant frontier garrison duty, and many people fled to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 富陽民唐□之因以妖術惑眾作亂，攻陷富陽，三吳卻籍者奔之，眾至三萬。

translations.literal: The Fuyang commoner Tang [—] thereupon used sorcery to delude the masses and raise rebellion, captured Fuyang, and those in the Three Wu region whose registers had been rejected flocked to him until his force reached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyang commoner Tang Yuzhi thereupon used sorcery to delude the people and raise a rebellion, captured Fuyang, and those in the Three Wu region whose registry entries had been rejected rallied to him until his force reached thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 文度與茹法亮、呂文顯皆以奸諂有寵於上。

translations.literal: Wendu, together with Ru Faliang and Lü Wenxian, all won favor with the emperor through treachery and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu, together with Ru Faliang and Lü Wenxian, all won the emperor's favor through treachery and flattery.

sentences.zh: 文度為外監，專制兵權，領軍守虛位而已。

translations.literal: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor, monopolized military authority, and the Commander-in-Chief held only an empty title.
translations.idiomatic: As Outer Supervisor, Wendu monopolized military authority, while the Commander-in-Chief held only an empty title.

sentences.zh: 法亮為中書通事舍人，權勢尤盛。

translations.literal: Faliang served as Palace Attendant for General Affairs of the Secretariat, and his power was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang served as Palace Attendant for General Affairs of the Secretariat, and his power was especially great.

sentences.zh: 王儉常曰：「我雖有大位，權寄豈及茹公邪！」

translations.literal: Wang Jian often said, "Though I hold a great office, how could the delegation of power compare with Master Ru!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian often said, "Though I hold a great office, how could the delegation of power compare with Master Ru!"

sentences.zh: 是歲，柔然部真可汗卒，子豆侖立，號伏名敦可汗，改元太平。

translations.literal: That year, Rouran Khan Bu Zhen died; his son Dou Lun succeeded him, took the title Khan Fumingdun, and changed the era name to Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: That year Rouran Khan Bu Zhen died; his son Dou Lun succeeded him, took the title Khan Fumingdun, and changed the era name to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 4 (

sentences.zh: 丙寅，公元四八六年）

translations.literal: bingyin, the year 486 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingyin, the year 486 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸亥朔，魏高祖朝會，始服袞冕。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the guihai new moon, Wei Emperor Gaozu held court assembly and for the first time wore the robe and cap of state.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the guihai new moon, Northern Wei Emperor Gaozu held court and for the first time wore the robe and cap of state.

sentences.zh: 壬午，柔然寇魏邊。

translations.literal: On renwu, Rouran raided the Wei frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Rouran raided the Northern Wei frontier.

sentences.zh: 唐□之攻陷錢唐，吳郡諸縣令多棄城走。

translations.literal: Tang [—] captured Qiantang, and many county magistrates of Wu Commandery abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuzhi captured Qiantang, and many county magistrates of Wu Commandery abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: □之稱帝於錢唐，立太子，置百官；

translations.literal: [—] Zhi declared himself emperor at Qiantang, installed a crown prince, and established the full bureaucracy;
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi declared himself emperor at Qiantang, installed a crown prince, and established a full bureaucracy;

sentences.zh: 遣其將高道度等攻陷東陽，殺東陽太守蕭崇之。

translations.literal: he sent his generals Gao Daodu and others to capture Dongyang and kill Dongyang Administrator Xiao Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: he sent his generals Gao Daodu and others to capture Dongyang and kill Dongyang Administrator Xiao Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 崇之，太祖族弟也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi was a clansman of the Founding Emperor's generation.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi was a clansman of the Founding Emperor's generation.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將孫泓寇山陰，至浦陽江，浹口戍主湯休武擊破之。

translations.literal: He also sent his general Sun Hong to raid Shanyin; when they reached the Puyang River, Jiekou Garrison Commander Tang Xiuwu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his general Sun Hong to raid Shanyin; when they reached the Puyang River, Jiekou Garrison Commander Tang Xiuwu defeated them.

sentences.zh: 上發禁兵數千人，馬數百匹，東擊□之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched several thousand palace troops and several hundred horses east to attack [—] Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched several thousand palace troops and several hundred horses east to attack Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 台軍至錢唐，□之眾烏合，畏騎兵，一戰而潰，擒斬□之，進平諸郡縣。

translations.literal: When the capital army reached Qiantang, [—] Zhi's force was a rabble; fearing cavalry, they collapsed in a single battle; [—] Zhi was captured and executed, and the army advanced to pacify the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital army reached Qiantang, Yuzhi's force was a rabble; terrified of the cavalry, they collapsed in a single battle; Yuzhi was captured and executed, and the army went on to pacify the commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 台軍乘勝，頗縱抄掠。

translations.literal: The capital army, riding its victory, largely allowed looting.
translations.idiomatic: The capital army, riding its victory, largely allowed looting.

sentences.zh: 軍還，上聞之，丁酉，收軍主前軍將軍陳天福棄市；

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor learned of it; on dingyou he had Army Commander Former Army General Chen Tianfu executed in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor learned of it; on dingyou he had Army Commander Former Army General Chen Tianfu executed in the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍劉明徹免官、削爵，付東冶。

translations.literal: Left Army General Liu Mingche was removed from office, stripped of his noble rank, and sent to the Eastern Works.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army General Liu Mingche was removed from office, stripped of his noble rank, and sent to the Eastern Works.

sentences.zh: 天福，上寵將也，既伏誅，內外莫不震肅。

translations.literal: Tianfu was a favored general of the emperor; once he had been executed, none within or without failed to be awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu was one of the emperor's favored generals; once he had been executed, everyone inside and outside the court was awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 使通事舍人丹陽劉系宗隨軍慰勞，遍至遭賊郡縣，百姓被驅逼者悉無所問。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Attendant for General Affairs Liu Xizong of Danyang to follow the army and offer consolation; going everywhere to the commanderies and counties that had suffered the rebels, he questioned none of the common people who had been coerced.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Attendant for General Affairs Liu Xizong of Danyang to follow the army and offer consolation; traveling to every commandery and county that had suffered the rebels, he questioned none of the common people who had been coerced.

sentences.zh: 閏月，癸巳，立皇子子貞為邵陵王，皇孫昭文為臨汝公。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on guisi, the emperor invested his son Zizhen as Prince of Shaoling and his grandson Zhaowen as Duke of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guisi, the emperor invested his son Zizhen as Prince of Shaoling and his grandson Zhaowen as Duke of Linru.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊後起卒。

translations.literal: Di King Yang Houqi died.
translations.idiomatic: Di King Yang Houqi died.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔以白水太守楊集始為北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: On dingwei, an edict appointed Baishui Administrator Yang Jishi as Inspector of North Qin Province and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei an edict appointed Baishui Administrator Yang Jishi as Inspector of North Qin Province and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 集始，文弘之子也。

translations.literal: Jishi was the son of Wenhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi was the son of Wenhong.

sentences.zh: 後起弟後明為白水太守。

translations.literal: Houqi's younger brother Houming served as Administrator of Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: Houqi's younger brother Houming served as Administrator of Baishui.

sentences.zh: 魏亦以集始為武都王。

translations.literal: Wei also made Jishi King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei also recognized Jishi as King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 集始入朝於魏，魏以為南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Jishi entered court audience in Wei, and Wei appointed him Inspector of South Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Jishi went to court in Northern Wei, he was appointed Inspector of South Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上耕籍田。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 二月，己未，立皇弟金求為晉熙王，鉉為河東王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiwei, the emperor invested his younger brother Jinqiu as Prince of Jinxi and Xuan as Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiwei, the emperor invested his younger brother Jinqiu as Prince of Jinxi and Xuan as Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 魏無鄉黨之法，唯立宗主督護；

translations.literal: Wei had no village-and-ward system, but only established clan chiefs as overseers;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei had no village-and-ward system, but only clan chiefs serving as overseers;

sentences.zh: 民多隱冒，三五十家始為一戶。

translations.literal: the people widely concealed and misregistered themselves, and only thirty or fifty households made up a single registered household.
translations.idiomatic: the people widely concealed themselves and misregistered their households, so that thirty or fifty families might be counted as a single household.

sentences.zh: 內秘書令李衝上言：「宜准古法：五家立鄰長，五鄰立里長，五里立黨長，取鄉人強謹者為之。

translations.literal: Inner Secretariat Director Li Chong memorialized: "It is fitting to follow the ancient law: five households establish a neighborhood chief, five neighborhoods a hamlet chief, five hamlets a party chief, choosing strong and conscientious men of the locality for the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Secretariat Director Li Chong submitted a memorial: "We should follow the ancient law: every five households should appoint a neighborhood chief, every five neighborhoods a hamlet chief, and every five hamlets a party chief, choosing strong and conscientious local men for the posts.

sentences.zh: 鄰長復一夫，里長二夫，黨長三夫；

translations.literal: A neighborhood chief is exempt one corvée laborer, a hamlet chief two, a party chief three;
translations.idiomatic: A neighborhood chief would be exempt one corvée laborer, a hamlet chief two, and a party chief three;

sentences.zh: 三載無過，則升一等。

translations.literal: after three years without fault, they are promoted one grade.
translations.idiomatic: after three years without fault, they would be promoted one grade.

sentences.zh: 其民調，一夫一婦，帛一匹，粟二石。

translations.literal: For the people's tax levy, one male and one female owed one bolt of silk and two shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: For the people's tax levy, each household of one male and one female would owe one bolt of silk and two shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 大率十匹為公調，二匹為調外費，三匹為百官俸。

translations.literal: Roughly, ten bolts formed the public levy, two bolts extra fees on the levy, and three bolts official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly speaking, ten bolts would go to the public levy, two bolts to extra fees on the levy, and three bolts to official salaries.

sentences.zh: 此外復有雜調。

translations.literal: Beyond this there were also miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this there were also miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 民年八十已上，聽一子不從役。

translations.literal: Commoners eighty years of age and above were permitted one son to be exempt from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners aged eighty or above were permitted one son to be exempt from corvée.

sentences.zh: 孤獨、癃老、篤疾、貧窮不能自存者，三長內迭養食之。」

translations.literal: The orphaned, aged, seriously ill, and destitute who could not support themselves were to be fed in rotation among the three chiefs."
translations.idiomatic: Orphans, the aged, the seriously ill, and the destitute who could not support themselves were to be supported in rotation by the three chiefs."

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔百官通議。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered all officials to discuss it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered all officials to discuss it jointly.

sentences.zh: 中書令鄭羲等皆以為不可。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zheng Xi and others all held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Zheng Xi and others all held that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 太尉丕曰：「臣謂此法若行，於公私有益。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Pi said, "Your servant considers that if this law is carried out, it will benefit both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan Pi said, "Your servant considers that if this law is carried out, it will benefit both public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 但方有事之月，校比戶口，民必勞怨。
