translations.literal: But just when there are active campaigns, to verify and compare household registers will surely weary and anger the people.
translations.idiomatic: But just when campaigns are underway, verifying and comparing household registers will surely weary and anger the people.

sentences.zh: 請過今秋，至冬乃遣使者，於事為宜。」

translations.literal: I ask that we pass this autumn and only in winter send out envoys; that would be fitting for the matter."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we wait until after this autumn and only send out envoys in winter; that would be more fitting."

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「『民可使由之，不可使知之。』

translations.literal: Chong said, "'The people may be made to follow it; they may not be made to understand it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "'The people may be made to follow it; they may not be made to understand it.

sentences.zh: 若不因調時，民徒知立長校戶之勤，未見均徭省賦之益，心必生怨。

translations.literal: If we do not do it at tax-collection time, the people will only know the toil of establishing chiefs and verifying households, and will not yet see the benefit of equal corvée and reduced levies; resentment will surely arise in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not do it at tax-collection time, the people will only know the toil of establishing chiefs and verifying households, and will not yet see the benefit of equal corvée and reduced levies; resentment will surely arise in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 宜及課調之月，令知賦稅之均，既識其事，又得其利，行之差易。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to do it in the month of tax assessment and collection, so that they know the taxes are equalized; once they understand the matter and also gain the benefit, carrying it out will be somewhat easier."
translations.idiomatic: We should do it in the month of tax assessment and collection, so that the people know their taxes are equalized; once they understand the matter and also gain the benefit, implementation will be much easier."

sentences.zh: 群臣多言：「九品差調，為日已久，一旦改法，恐成擾亂。」

translations.literal: Many ministers said, "The nine-rank gradated levy has been in force a long time; to change the law at once may cause disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers said, "The nine-rank gradated levy has been in force a long time; to change the law at once may cause disorder."

sentences.zh: 文明太后曰：「立三長則課調有常准，苞廕之戶可出，僥倖之人可止，何為不可！」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming said, "If the three chiefs are established, tax levies will have a fixed standard, sheltered dependent households can be brought out, and opportunists can be stopped—why should it not be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming said, "If the three chiefs are established, tax levies will have a fixed standard, sheltered dependent households can be brought into the open, and opportunists can be stopped—why should it not be done!"

sentences.zh: 甲戌，初立黨、裡、鄰三長，定民戶籍。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the party, hamlet, and neighborhood three chiefs were first established, and the people's household registers were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the party, hamlet, and neighborhood three chiefs were first established, and the people's household registers were fixed.

sentences.zh: 民始皆愁苦，豪強者尤不願。

translations.literal: At first the people were all distressed and bitter, and the powerful especially did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people were all distressed and bitter, and the powerful especially did not wish it.

sentences.zh: 既而課調省費十餘倍，上下安之。

translations.literal: Before long tax levies were reduced in cost by more than tenfold, and high and low alike were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long tax levies fell to less than a tenth of their former cost, and high and low alike were content.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙申，柔然遣使者牟提如魏。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingshen, Rouran sent the envoy Muti to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, Rouran sent the envoy Muti to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 時敕勒叛柔然，柔然伏名敦可汗自將討之，追奔至西漠。

translations.literal: At that time the Tiele rebelled against Rouran; Rouran Khan Fumingdun personally led a campaign against them and pursued the fugitives to the Western Desert.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tiele rebelled against Rouran; Rouran Khan Fumingdun personally led a campaign against them and pursued the fugitives to the Western Desert.

sentences.zh: 魏左僕射穆亮等請乘虛擊之，中書監高閭曰：「秦、漢之世，海內一統，故可遠征匈奴。

translations.literal: Wei Left Vice Director Mu Liang and others asked to strike them while they were exposed; Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lü said, "In the Qin and Han ages, the realm within the seas was unified, and so one could campaign far against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Left Vice Director Mu Liang and others asked to strike while Rouran was exposed; Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lü said, "In the Qin and Han ages the realm within the seas was unified, and so one could campaign far against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 今南有吳寇，何可捨之深入虜庭！」

translations.literal: Now in the south there is the Wu invader—how can we abandon that and plunge deep into the barbarian court!"
translations.idiomatic: Now we have the Wu invader in the south—how can we abandon that and plunge deep into the barbarian heartland!"

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「『兵者凶器，聖人不得已而用之。』

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "'Arms are an ill-omened instrument; the sage uses them only when he has no choice.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor said, "'Arms are an ill-omened instrument; the sage uses them only when he has no choice.

sentences.zh: 先帝屢出征伐者，以有未賓之虜故也。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor repeatedly went on campaign because there were barbarians not yet brought to submission.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor repeatedly went on campaign because there were barbarians not yet brought to submission.

sentences.zh: 今朕承太平之業，奈何無故動兵革乎！」

translations.literal: Now I inherit a realm of peace—how can I for no reason set arms in motion!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I inherit a realm at peace—how can I for no reason set arms in motion!"

sentences.zh: 厚禮其使者而歸之。

translations.literal: He treated their envoy with generous rites and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the Rouran envoy with generous rites and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛酉朔，魏始制五等公服；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinyou new moon, Wei first established the five-rank public robes;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinyou new moon, Northern Wei first established the five-rank public robes;

sentences.zh: 甲子，初以法服、御輦祀西郊。

translations.literal: On jiazi, for the first time he used ritual robes and the imperial carriage to sacrifice at the Western Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he for the first time wore ritual robes and rode the imperial carriage to sacrifice at the Western Suburb.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏主如靈泉池。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Wei ruler went to Spirit Spring Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the Northern Wei emperor went to Spirit Spring Pool.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，還宮。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 湘州蠻反，刺史呂安國有疾不能討；

translations.literal: The barbarians of Xiang Province rebelled, and the inspector Lü Anguo was ill and could not suppress them;
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Xiang Province rose in revolt, and Inspector Lü Anguo, who was ill, could not put them down;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以尚書左僕射柳世隆為湘州刺史，討平之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Liu Shilong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Inspector of Xiang Province and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Liu Shilong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Inspector of Xiang Province and brought the rebellion to an end.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，魏主如方山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinyou, the Wei ruler went to Fang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinyou, the Northern Wei emperor went to Fang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏文明太后賜皇子恂名，大赦。

translations.literal: On jimao, Empress Dowager Wenming of Wei bestowed a name on the imperial prince Xun and issued a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Empress Dowager Wenming of Northern Wei gave the imperial prince Xun his name and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊戌，魏主如方山。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuxu, the Wei ruler went to Fang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuxu, the Northern Wei emperor again went to Fang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥，魏給尚書五等爵已上朱衣、玉珮、大小組綬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yihai, Wei granted to Masters of Writing of the fifth rank of nobility and above vermilion robes, jade pendants, and large and small ribbon seals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yihai, Northern Wei granted vermilion robes, jade pendants, and graded ribbon seals to Masters of Writing of the fifth rank of nobility and above.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛卯，魏作明堂、辟雍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinmao, Wei built the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinmao, Northern Wei constructed the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，魏議定民官依戶給俸。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Wei deliberated and fixed salaries for civil officials according to households.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Northern Wei decided that civil officials' salaries should be allotted according to the number of households under their charge.

sentences.zh: 十二月，柔然寇魏邊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Rouran raided Wei's borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Rouran raided the Northern Wei frontier.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏改中書學曰國子學。

translations.literal: That year, Wei changed the Directorate of Literature School to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: That year Northern Wei renamed the Directorate of Literature School the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 分置州郡，凡三十八州，二十五在河南，十三在河北。

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies were divided and established; in all there were thirty-eight provinces, twenty-five south of the Yellow River and thirteen north of it.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies were reorganized into thirty-eight provinces in all, twenty-five south of the Yellow River and thirteen north of it.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 5 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 5 (

sentences.zh: 丁卯，公元四八七年）

translations.literal: dingmao, the year 487 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingmao, the year 487 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥朔，魏主詔定樂章，非雅者除之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dinghai, the first day of the month, the Wei ruler issued an edict fixing the musical compositions and removing those that were not elegant.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dinghai, the new moon, the Northern Wei emperor issued an edict standardizing the court music and abolishing pieces that were not properly refined.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以豫章王嶷為大司馬，章陵王子良為司徒，臨川王映、衛將軍王儉、中軍將軍王敬則並加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Prince of Yuzhang Niao was made Grand Marshal, Ziliang of Prince of Zhangling was made Minister over the Masses, and Prince of Linchuan Ying, General of the Guards Wang Jian, and General of the Central Army Wang Jingze were all given the added title of Grand General with staff equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Prince Niao of Yuzhang was appointed Grand Marshal, Xiao Ziliang of Prince of Zhangling was made Minister over the Masses, and Prince Ying of Linchuan, General of the Guards Wang Jian, and General of the Central Army Wang Jingze were all granted the added title of Grand General with staff equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 子良啟記室范雲為郡，上曰：「聞其常相賣弄，朕不復窮法，當宥之以遠。」

translations.literal: Ziliang recommended his recorder Fan Yun for a commandery post. The emperor said, "I have heard that he often trades on cleverness; I will not pursue the law to the end and shall pardon him by sending him far away."
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang recommended his chief clerk Fan Yun for a commandery appointment. The emperor said, "I have heard that he is always showing off his wit; I will not press the charge to the full extent of the law and shall pardon him by sending him far away."

sentences.zh: 子良曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Ziliang said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 雲動相規誨，諫書具存。」

translations.literal: Yun constantly admonished and instructed me, and his remonstrances are all preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun constantly counseled and admonished me, and his memorials of remonstrance are all still preserved."

sentences.zh: 遂取以奏，凡百餘紙，辭皆切直。

translations.literal: He then took them and presented them; in all there were more than a hundred sheets, and the language in every case was sharp and direct.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought them forward for presentation; there were more than a hundred sheets in all, and every word was forthright and incisive.

sentences.zh: 上歎息，謂子良曰：「不謂雲能爾；

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said to Ziliang, "I did not think Yun could be like this;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said to Ziliang, "I never thought Fan Yun capable of this;

sentences.zh: 方使弼汝，何宜出守！」

translations.literal: I was just about to have him assist you—how could he be sent out to guard a commandery!"
translations.idiomatic: I was just about to have him assist you—how could he be sent away to govern a commandery!"

sentences.zh: 文惠太子嘗出東田觀獲，顧謂眾賓曰：「刈此亦殊可觀。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhu once went out to the Eastern Fields to watch the harvest and, turning to the assembled guests, said, "Cutting this is also quite worth seeing."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhu once went out to the Eastern Fields to watch the harvest and, turning to the assembled guests, said, "Watching this reaping is really quite a sight."

sentences.zh: 眾皆唯唯，雲獨曰：「三時之務，實為長勤。

translations.literal: All murmured agreement, but Yun alone said, "The labors of the three seasons are truly long and arduous.
translations.idiomatic: All murmured agreement, but Fan Yun alone said, "The work of the three farming seasons is truly unending toil.

sentences.zh: 伏願殿下知稼穡之艱難，無徇一朝之宴逸。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Highness will understand the hardship of sowing and reaping and not indulge a single morning's feasting and ease."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Highness to understand how hard it is to grow grain and not indulge a single morning's feasting and idleness."

sentences.zh: 荒人桓天生自稱桓玄宗族，與雍、司二州蠻相扇動，據南陽故城，請兵於魏，將入寇。

translations.literal: The wilderness man Huan Tiansheng declared himself a clansman of the Huan clan of the Xuan era, stirred up the barbarians of Yong and Si provinces together with him, seized the old city of Nanyang, requested troops from Wei, and was about to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tiansheng, a frontier tribesman, claimed descent from the Huan clan of the Eastern Jin, incited the tribal peoples of Yong and Si provinces to join him, seized the old city of Nanyang, asked Northern Wei for troops, and prepared to invade Qi.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔假丹陽尹蕭景先節，總帥步騎，直指義陽，司州諸軍皆受節度；

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict temporarily granted the seal of authority to Xiao Jingxian, Intendant of Danyang, to command infantry and cavalry in chief, strike directly at Yiyang, and all armies of Si Province were to accept his command;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou an edict temporarily granted the seal of authority to Xiao Jingxian, Intendant of Danyang, to take overall command of infantry and cavalry and march straight on Yiyang, with all armies of Si Province placed under his authority;

sentences.zh: 又假護軍將軍陳顯達節，帥征虜將軍戴僧靜等水軍向宛、葉，雍、司眾軍皆受顯達節度，以討之。

translations.literal: It also temporarily granted the seal of authority to Protector-General Chen Xianda, who led the river forces of General Who Conquers the Barbarians Dai Sengjing and others toward Wan and Ye; all armies of Yong and Si were to accept Xianda's command, to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: It also temporarily granted the seal of authority to Protector-General Chen Xianda, who led a river force under General Who Conquers the Barbarians Dai Sengjing and others toward Wan and Ye, with all armies of Yong and Si placed under Xianda's command to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 魏光祿大夫咸陽文公高允，歷事五帝，出入三省，五十餘年，未嘗有譴；

translations.literal: Gao Yun, Grandee of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Literature of Xianyang in Wei, served five emperors, entering and leaving the Three Departments for more than fifty years without ever once being rebuked;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun of Northern Wei, Grandee of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Literature of Xianyang, served five emperors and moved in and out of the Three Departments for more than fifty years without ever once being rebuked;

sentences.zh: 馮太后及魏主甚重之，常命中黃門蘇興壽扶侍。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng and the Wei ruler greatly valued him and often ordered the Palace Attendant Su Xingshou to support and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng and the Northern Wei emperor held him in the highest regard and often ordered Palace Attendant Su Xingshou to support and attend him.

sentences.zh: 允仁恕簡靜，雖處貴重，情同寒素；

translations.literal: Yun was benevolent, forgiving, simple, and quiet; though he occupied a lofty and honored position, his feelings were those of the poor and plain;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun was benevolent, forgiving, plain, and quiet; though he held a lofty and honored position, he lived as simply as a poor commoner;

sentences.zh: 執書吟覽，晝夜不去手，誨人以善，恂恂不倦；

translations.literal: he held books, recited and read them, day and night never letting them leave his hands, taught others goodness, and was modest and untiring;
translations.idiomatic: he held books in his hands day and night, reading and reciting without pause, taught others to do good, and was modest and untiring;

sentences.zh: 篤親念故，無所遺棄。

translations.literal: he was deeply devoted to kin and mindful of old friends and abandoned no one.
translations.idiomatic: he was deeply devoted to his kin and mindful of old friends and abandoned no one.

sentences.zh: 顯祖平青、徐，悉徙其望族於代，其人多允之婚媾，流離饑寒；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu pacified Qing and Xu, he moved all their eminent clans to Dai; many of them were connected to Yun by marriage and were scattered, starving, and cold;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu pacified Qing and Xu, he relocated all their eminent clans to Dai; many of them were related to Gao Yun by marriage and were scattered, starving, and destitute;

sentences.zh: 允傾家賑施，鹹得其所，又隨其才行，薦之於朝。

translations.literal: Yun emptied his household to give relief, and all obtained their proper place; he also, according to each person's talent and conduct, recommended them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun emptied his household to give relief until all had found their proper place, and he also recommended them to the court according to each person's talent and character.

sentences.zh: 議者多以初附間之，允曰：「任賢使能，何有新舊！

translations.literal: Critics often used their recent submission to cast doubt on them. Yun said, "In appointing the worthy and employing the able, what difference is there between old and new!
translations.idiomatic: Critics often used their recent submission to cast doubt on them. Gao Yun said, "When appointing the worthy and employing the able, what difference is there between old subjects and new!

sentences.zh: 必若有用，豈可以此抑之！」

translations.literal: If they are truly useful, how can one suppress them for this reason!"
translations.idiomatic: If they are truly useful, how can one hold them back for that reason alone!"

sentences.zh: 允體素無疾，至是微有不適，猶起居如常，數日而卒，年九十八。

translations.literal: Yun's constitution had always been free of illness; at this time he had a slight indisposition, yet he still rose and retired as usual, and after several days he died, aged ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun had always enjoyed robust health; now he felt slightly unwell, yet he still went about his daily routine as usual, and after several days he died at the age of ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空，賻襚甚厚；

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, and the funeral gifts and shrouds were very generous;
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, and the funeral gifts and burial accoutrements were exceedingly generous;

sentences.zh: 魏初以來，存亡蒙賚，皆莫及也。

translations.literal: from the beginning of Wei, none who received gifts in life or death could compare.
translations.idiomatic: since the founding of Northern Wei, no one who had received imperial gifts in life or death had ever been honored so richly.

sentences.zh: 桓天生引魏兵萬餘人至沘陽，陳顯達遣戴僧靜等與戰於深橋，大破之，殺獲萬計。

translations.literal: Huan Tiansheng led more than ten thousand Wei troops to Biyang. Chen Xianda sent Dai Sengjing and others to fight them at Shenqiao, routed them utterly, and killed and captured men by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tiansheng led more than ten thousand Northern Wei troops to Biyang. Chen Xianda sent Dai Sengjing and others to engage them at Shenqiao, routed them completely, and killed and captured men by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 天生退保沘陽，僧靜圍之，不克而還。

translations.literal: Tiansheng withdrew to hold Biyang. Sengjing besieged it but could not take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng withdrew to hold Biyang. Dai Sengjing besieged the city but failed to take it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 荒人胡丘生起兵懸瓠以應齊，魏人擊破之，丘生來奔。

translations.literal: The wilderness man Hu Qiusheng raised troops at Xuanhuo to respond to Qi. The Wei men routed him, and Qiusheng came over in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier tribesman Hu Qiusheng raised troops at Xuanhuo in support of Qi. Northern Wei forces defeated him, and Qiusheng fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 天生又引魏兵寇舞陰，舞陰戍主殷公愍拒擊破之，殺其副張麒麟，天生被創退走。

translations.literal: Tiansheng again led Wei troops to raid Wuyin. Yin Gongmin, garrison commander of Wuyin, repulsed and defeated them, killed his lieutenant Zhang Qilin, and Tiansheng, wounded, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng again led Northern Wei troops to raid Wuyin. Yin Gongmin, garrison commander of Wuyin, repulsed and defeated them, killed his lieutenant Zhang Qilin, and Tiansheng, wounded, fled.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁未，以陳顯達為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingwei, Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingwei, Chen Xianda was appointed Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 顯達進據舞陽城。

translations.literal: Xianda advanced and occupied Wuyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda advanced and occupied Wuyang city.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬辰，魏主如靈泉池。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on renchen, the Wei ruler went to Spirit Spring Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on renchen, the Northern Wei emperor went to Spirit Spring Pool.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，魏南平王渾卒。

translations.literal: On guisi, Prince of Nanping Hun of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Yuan Hun, Prince of Nanping in Northern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔復七廟子孫及外戚緦麻服已上，賦役無所與。

translations.literal: An edict restored exemption from levies and corvée to descendants of the seven temples and maternal relatives wearing mourning of the highest grade and above.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored exemption from taxes and corvée to descendants of the seven temples and maternal relatives in the highest grade of mourning and above.

sentences.zh: 魏南部尚書公孫邃、上谷公張儵帥眾與桓天生復寇舞陰，殷公愍擊破之；

translations.literal: Gongsun Sui, Southern Director of the Masters of Writing of Wei, and Zhang Chu, Duke of Shanggu, led their forces together with Huan Tiansheng to raid Wuyin again. Yin Gongmin repulsed and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Sui, Southern Director of the Masters of Writing of Northern Wei, and Zhang Chu, Duke of Shanggu, led their forces together with Huan Tiansheng to raid Wuyin again. Yin Gongmin repulsed and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 天生還竄荒中。

translations.literal: Tiansheng again fled back into the wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng again fled back into the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 邃，表之孫也。

translations.literal: Sui was a grandson of Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Sui was a grandson of Gongsun Biao.

sentences.zh: 魏春夏大旱，代地尤甚；

translations.literal: In Wei there was great drought in spring and summer, and the Dai region was especially severe;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei suffered severe drought in spring and summer, and the Dai region was hit hardest;

sentences.zh: 加以牛疫，民餒死者多。

translations.literal: added to this was cattle plague, and many of the people died of famine.
translations.idiomatic: cattle plague compounded the disaster, and many people died of famine.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸未，詔內外之臣極言無隱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiwei, an edict ordered inner and outer officials to speak to the utmost without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiwei, an edict ordered officials at court and in the provinces to speak frankly without holding anything back.

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史韓麒麟上表曰：「古先哲王，儲積九稔；

translations.literal: Han Qilin, Inspector of Qi Province, submitted a memorial saying, "The sage kings of antiquity stored up grain for nine harvests;
translations.idiomatic: Han Qilin, Inspector of Qi Province, submitted a memorial saying, "The sage kings of antiquity stored grain for nine harvests;

sentences.zh: 逮於中代，亦崇斯業，入粟者與斬敵同爵，力田者與孝悌均賞。

translations.literal: down to the middle ages they also honored this practice: those who contributed grain received the same rank as those who beheaded enemies, and those who worked the fields diligently received the same reward as those who practiced filial piety and brotherliness.
translations.idiomatic: down through the middle ages they also honored this practice: those who contributed grain received the same rank as those who beheaded enemies in battle, and those who worked the fields diligently received the same rewards as those who practiced filial piety and brotherliness.

sentences.zh: 今京師民庶，不田者多，游食之口，三分居二。

translations.literal: Now among the common people of the capital, many do not farm; mouths living idly make up two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the capital, many commoners do not farm at all; idlers who live without working make up two-thirds of the population.

sentences.zh: 自承平日久，豐穰積年，競相矜誇，遂成侈俗。

translations.literal: Since peace has lasted long, harvests have been abundant year after year, people compete in boasting, and an extravagant custom has formed.
translations.idiomatic: Since peace has lasted so long and harvests have been abundant year after year, people compete in display and extravagance until it has become the custom.

sentences.zh: 貴富之家，童妾袨服，工商之族，僕隸玉食，而農夫闕糟糠，蠶婦乏短褐。

translations.literal: In noble and wealthy households, young concubines wear splendid clothes; among merchant and artisan families, servants and slaves eat jade-like fare, while farmers lack coarse grain and silkworm-raising women lack short hemp garments.
translations.idiomatic: In noble and wealthy households young concubines dress in splendid clothes; among merchant and artisan families servants and slaves eat delicacies, while farmers go without coarse grain and women who raise silkworms lack even short hemp garments.

sentences.zh: 故耕者日少，田有荒蕪；

translations.literal: Therefore those who plow grow fewer day by day, and fields lie abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: As a result those who farm grow fewer by the day, and fields lie abandoned;

sentences.zh: 谷帛罄於府庫，寶貨盈於市裡；

translations.literal: grain and cloth are exhausted in the treasuries, while precious goods overflow in the marketplaces;
translations.idiomatic: grain and cloth are exhausted in the treasuries while precious goods overflow in the marketplaces;

sentences.zh: 衣食匱於室，麗服溢於路。

translations.literal: food and clothing are scarce in the home, while fine garments spill into the roads.
translations.idiomatic: food and clothing are scarce within homes while fine garments spill into the streets.

sentences.zh: 饑寒之本，實在於斯。

translations.literal: The root of hunger and cold truly lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The root of hunger and cold truly lies here.

sentences.zh: 愚謂凡珍異之物，皆宜禁斷，吉凶之禮，備為格式；

translations.literal: I humbly hold that all rare and exotic goods should be forbidden and cut off, and rites of auspice and mourning should be fully set in fixed forms;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe that all rare and exotic goods should be banned, and that rites for auspicious and mourning occasions should be fully codified;

sentences.zh: 勸課農桑，嚴加賞罰。

translations.literal: agriculture and sericulture should be encouraged and inspected, with rewards and punishments strictly applied.
translations.idiomatic: agriculture and sericulture should be encouraged and supervised, with rewards and punishments strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，必有盈贍。

translations.literal: Within several years there will surely be surplus and plenty.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years there will surely be surplus and abundance.

sentences.zh: 往年校比戶貫，租賦輕少。

translations.literal: In recent years household registers were checked and compared, and land tax and levies were light and small.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, when household registers were checked and compared, land taxes and levies were kept light.

sentences.zh: 臣所統齊州，租粟才可給俸，略無入倉，雖於民為利，而不可長久。

translations.literal: In Qi Province, which I govern, the grain rent barely suffices for salaries and scarcely enters the granaries; though this benefits the people, it cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Province, which I govern, grain rents barely cover official salaries and scarcely reach the granaries; though this benefits the people, it cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 脫有戎役，或遭天災，恐供給之方，無所取濟。

translations.literal: If there should be military campaigns or natural disasters, I fear there will be no source from which to draw for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: If war should break out or natural disaster strike, I fear there will be no reserve from which to draw for relief.

sentences.zh: 可減絹布，增益谷租；

translations.literal: Silk and cloth levies may be reduced and grain rents increased;
translations.idiomatic: Silk and cloth levies could be reduced and grain rents increased;

sentences.zh: 年豐多積，歲儉出賑。

translations.literal: in years of abundance store more, and in years of scarcity release for relief.
translations.idiomatic: store more in years of abundance and release grain for relief in years of scarcity.

sentences.zh: 所謂私民之谷，寄積於官，官有宿積，則民無荒年矣。」

translations.literal: This is what is meant by the people's private grain being deposited and stored with the state: when the state has long-standing stores, the people will have no famine years."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by letting the people's grain be stored by the state: when the government maintains long-standing reserves, the people will never know famine years."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，詔有司開倉賑貸，聽民出關就食。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, an edict ordered the relevant offices to open the granaries for relief loans and permitted the people to leave the passes to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, an edict ordered the relevant offices to open the granaries for relief loans and permitted the people to leave the frontier passes to seek food elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 遣使者造籍，分遣去留，所過給糧廩，所至三長贍養之。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to compile registers, assign who would leave and who would stay, supply grain stores along the route, and have the three chiefs at each place provide for them.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to compile registers, assign who would leave and who would remain, supply grain along the route, and have the local three-chief units provide for them wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 柔然伏名敦可汗殘暴，其臣侯醫垔石洛候數諫止之，且勸其與魏和親。

translations.literal: Fumingdun Khan of the Rouran was cruel and violent. His minister Houyi Aishiluohou repeatedly remonstrated to stop him and also urged him to seek marriage alliance with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Fumingdun Khan of the Rouran was cruel and violent. His minister Houyi Aishiluohou repeatedly remonstrated against this and also urged him to seek a marriage alliance with Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 伏名敦怒，族誅之，由是部眾離心。

translations.literal: Fumingdun was enraged and executed his entire clan, and from this the tribes lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Fumingdun was enraged and executed his entire clan, and from that point his followers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 八月，柔然寇魏邊，魏以尚書陸睿為都督，擊柔然，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Rouran raided Wei's borders. Wei made Lu Rui, Master of Writing, commander-in-chief, attacked the Rouran, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Rouran raided the Northern Wei frontier. Northern Wei appointed Lu Rui, Master of Writing, commander-in-chief, attacked the Rouran, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 睿，麗之子也。

translations.literal: Rui was a son of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rui was a son of Lu Li.

sentences.zh: 初，高車阿伏至羅有部落十餘萬，役屬柔然。

translations.literal: Earlier, Avtuoluo of the Gaoche had more than a hundred thousand tribesmen and was subject in service to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Avtuoluo of the Gaoche had more than a hundred thousand tribesmen and was subject to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 伏名敦之侵魏也，阿伏至羅諫，不聽。

translations.literal: When Fumingdun invaded Wei, Avtuoluo remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Fumingdun invaded Northern Wei, Avtuoluo remonstrated, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅怒，與從弟窮奇帥部落西走，至前部西北，自立為王。

translations.literal: Avtuoluo was enraged and, together with his younger cousin Qiongqi, led his tribes west, reaching the northwest of the Former Front, and declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Avtuoluo was enraged and, together with his younger cousin Qiongqi, led his tribes west to the northwest of the Former Front and declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 國人號曰「候婁匐勒」，夏言天子也；

translations.literal: The people of the state called him "Houlou Fule," which in Chinese speech means Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: His people called him "Houlou Fule," which in Chinese means Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 號窮奇曰「候倍」，夏言太子也。

translations.literal: they called Qiongqi "Houbei," which in Chinese speech means crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: they called Qiongqi "Houbei," which in Chinese means crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二人甚親睦，分部而立，阿伏至羅居北，窮奇居南。

translations.literal: The two were very close and affectionate, divided their parts and established themselves: Avtuoluo dwelt in the north and Qiongqi in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The two were very close and affectionate; they divided their domains and established separate camps, with Avtuoluo in the north and Qiongqi in the south.

sentences.zh: 伏名敦追擊之，屢為阿伏至羅所敗，乃引眾東徙。

translations.literal: Fumingdun pursued and attacked them but was repeatedly defeated by Avtuoluo, and so led his multitude east in migration.
translations.idiomatic: Fumingdun pursued and attacked them but was repeatedly defeated by Avtuoluo, and so led his followers east in migration.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛未，魏詔罷起部無益之作，出宮人不執機杼者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinwei, Wei issued an edict abolishing useless works of the Construction Office and releasing palace women who did not operate looms.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinwei, Northern Wei issued an edict abolishing useless construction projects and releasing palace women who did not operate looms.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁未，又詔罷尚方錦繡、綾羅之工；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei, another edict abolished the brocade, embroidery, damask, and gauze workshops of the Imperial Workshop;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei, another edict abolished the brocade, embroidery, damask, and gauze workshops of the Imperial Workshop;

sentences.zh: 四民欲造，任之無禁。

translations.literal: if the four classes of people wished to make such goods, they were permitted without prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: if people of the four classes wished to make such goods, they were free to do so without restriction.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏久無事，府藏盈積。

translations.literal: At this time Wei had long been free of warfare, and the treasuries were full and overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Northern Wei had long been free of warfare, and the treasuries were full to overflowing.

sentences.zh: 詔盡出御府衣服珍寶、太官雜器、太僕乘具、內庫弓矢刀鈐十分之八，外府衣物、繒布、絲纊非供國用者，以其太半班賚百司，下至工、商、皁隸，逮於六鎮邊戍，畿內鰥、寡、孤、獨、貧、癃，皆有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all imperial wardrobe garments and treasures, miscellaneous vessels of the Grand Provisioner, riding equipment of the Grand Servant, and bows, arrows, blades, and halberds of the inner storehouse—eight-tenths of them—be released, along with more than half of outer-storehouse clothing, silk cloth, and silk floss not required for state use, to be distributed in graded gifts to the hundred offices, down to artisans, merchants, and menials, reaching the six garrisons on the frontier and, within the capital region, widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, the poor, and the infirm, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that eight-tenths of the imperial wardrobe's garments and treasures, the Grand Provisioner's miscellaneous vessels, the Grand Servant's riding equipment, and the inner storehouse's bows, arrows, blades, and halberds be released, along with more than half of the outer storehouse's clothing, silk cloth, and silk floss not required for state use, to be distributed in graded gifts to the hundred offices, down to artisans, merchants, and menials, reaching the six frontier garrisons and, within the capital region, widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, the poor, and the infirm, each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 魏秘書令高祐、丞李彪奏請改《國書》編年為紀、傳、表、志，魏主從之。

translations.literal: Gao You, Director of the Secretariat of Wei, and Vice Director Li Biao memorialized asking that the National History, in annalistic form, be changed to annals, biographies, tables, and treatises. The Wei ruler approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You, Director of the Secretariat of Northern Wei, and Vice Director Li Biao memorialized asking that the National History, which had been written in annalistic form, be reorganized into annals, biographies, tables, and treatises. The Northern Wei emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 祐，允之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: You was a younger cousin of Yun on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You was a younger cousin of Gao Yun on the paternal side.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔彪與著作朗崔光改修《國書》。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered Biao and Editorial Director Cui Guang to revise the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict ordered Li Biao and Editorial Director Cui Guang to revise the National History.

sentences.zh: 光，道固之從孫也。

translations.literal: Guang was a grandnephew of Daogu.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang was a grandnephew of Cui Daogu.

sentences.zh: 魏主問高祐曰：「何以止盜？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler asked Gao You, "How can theft be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor asked Gao You, "How can theft be stopped?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔宋均立德，猛虎渡河；

translations.literal: He replied, "In former times Song Jun established virtue and tigers crossed the river;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In former times Song Jun established virtue and tigers crossed the river;

sentences.zh: 卓茂行化，蝗不入境。

translations.literal: Zhuo Mao practiced transformation and locusts did not enter his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Mao practiced benevolent governance and locusts did not enter his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 況盜賊，人也，苟守宰得人，治化有方，止之易矣。」

translations.literal: How much more so with thieves and robbers, who are human beings: if the prefects and magistrates are the right men and governance and transformation have proper methods, stopping them is easy."
translations.idiomatic: How much more so with thieves and robbers, who are human beings: if prefects and magistrates are the right men and governance is properly conducted, stopping them is easy."

sentences.zh: 祐又上疏言：「今之選舉，不採識治之優劣，專簡年勞之多少，斯非盡才之謂。

translations.literal: Gao You also submitted a memorial saying, "In today's selections they do not assess the superiority or inferiority of knowledge of governance; they rely solely on how much seniority and service a man has accumulated. This is not what is meant by employing talent to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You also submitted a memorial in which he said, "Present-day appointments do not weigh a candidate's grasp of governance, but rely solely on years of seniority and service. That is not true meritocracy.

sentences.zh: 宜停此薄藝，棄彼朽勞，唯才是舉，則官方斯穆。

translations.literal: One should stop this paltry skill-measuring, discard that rotten seniority, promote men solely for ability, and then the official ranks will be orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Stop measuring petty qualifications, disregard stale service records, and promote men solely for talent—then government will be well ordered.

sentences.zh: 又勳舊之臣，雖年勤可錄而才非撫民者，可加之以爵賞，不宜委之以方任，所謂王者可私人以財，不私人以官者也。」

translations.literal: Again, for meritorious old ministers, though years of diligence may be recorded but talent is not suited to governing the people, one may add to them titles and rewards, but should not entrust them with regional responsibilities—what is called "the sovereign may favor individuals with wealth, but not with office."
translations.idiomatic: As for old ministers with meritorious service, those whose diligence deserves recognition but whose abilities do not suit governing the people may be rewarded with titles and gifts, but should not be given charge of a province—that is what is meant when it is said a ruler may favor a man with wealth, but not with office."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 祐出為西兗州刺史，鎮滑台。

translations.literal: Gao You went out as regional inspector of West Yan Province and garrisoned Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You was sent out as regional inspector of West Yan Province and stationed at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 以郡國雖有學，縣、黨亦宜有之，乃命縣立講學，黨立小學。

translations.literal: Considering that although commanderies and kingdoms had schools, counties and districts should also have them, he ordered counties to establish lecture schools and districts to establish elementary schools.
translations.idiomatic: Since commanderies and kingdoms already had schools but counties and districts did not, he ordered counties to establish lecture academies and districts to establish elementary schools.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 6 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 6 (

sentences.zh: 戊辰，公元四八八年）

translations.literal: wuchen, the year 488 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuchen, corresponding to 488 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙未，魏詔：「犯死刑者，父母、祖父母年老，更無成人子孫，旁無期親者，具狀以聞。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiwei, Wei issued an edict: "Those convicted of capital offenses whose parents and grandparents are elderly and have no adult descendants, and who have no collateral relatives within the mourning circle, should have the circumstances fully reported."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yiwei, Northern Wei issued an edict: "When one convicted of a capital crime has elderly parents or grandparents, no adult descendants, and no close collateral kin, the full circumstances are to be reported."

sentences.zh: 初，皇子右衛將軍子響出繼豫章王嶷；

translations.literal: Earlier, the imperial prince and General of the Right Guard Zixiang was given in adoption to Prince of Yuzhang Liao;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the imperial prince Zixiang, General of the Right Guard, had been given in adoption to Prince of Yuzhang Liao;

sentences.zh: 嶷後有子，表留為世子。

translations.literal: After Liao later had a son, he memorialized to retain him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao later had a son of his own, he memorialized asking to keep that son as his heir.

sentences.zh: 子響每入朝，以車服異於諸王，每拳擊車壁。

translations.literal: Each time Zixiang entered court, because his carriage and raiment differed from the other princes, each time he struck the carriage wall with his fist.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zixiang came to court he found his carriage and dress inferior to those of the other princes, and each time he would pound the carriage wall with his fist.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，詔車服與皇子同。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he issued an edict that his carriage and raiment were to be the same as an imperial prince's.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he decreed that Zixiang's carriage and dress should be the same as those of an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏子響宜還本。

translations.literal: Thereupon the relevant offices memorialized that Zixiang should return to his original status.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices thereupon memorialized that Zixiang should be restored to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 三月，己亥，立子響為巴東王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jihai, Zixiang was established as Prince of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jihai, Zixiang was enfeoffed as Prince of Badong.

sentences.zh: 角城戍將張蒲，因大霧乘船入清中採樵，潛納魏兵。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Jiaocheng, Zhang Pu, taking advantage of heavy fog, took boats into the Qing to gather firewood and secretly admitted Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu, garrison commander of Jiaocheng, took advantage of heavy fog to sail into the Qing River to gather firewood and secretly let Northern Wei troops in.

sentences.zh: 戍主皇甫仲賢覺之，帥眾拒戰於門中，僅能卻之。

translations.literal: The garrison chief Huangfu Zhongxian detected it, led the troops to resist battle at the gate, and barely managed to repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison chief Huangfu Zhongxian discovered the plot, led his men to fight them at the gate, and barely managed to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 魏步騎三千餘人已至塹外，淮陰軍主王僧慶等引兵救之，魏人乃退。

translations.literal: More than three thousand Wei infantry and cavalry had already reached outside the moat; Wang Sengqing of Huaiyin and others led troops to rescue them, and the Wei men then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand Northern Wei infantry and cavalry had already reached the far side of the moat; Wang Sengqing of Huaiyin and others led troops to the relief, and the Wei forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，桓天生復引魏兵出據隔城，詔游擊將軍下邳曹虎督諸軍討之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Huan Tiansheng again led Wei troops out to seize Gecheng; an edict ordered Mobile Corps General Cao Hu of Xiapi to direct the various armies to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Huan Tiansheng again brought Northern Wei troops out to occupy Gecheng; the emperor ordered Mobile Corps General Cao Hu of Xiapi to command the armies against him.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍朱公恩將兵翕伏，遇天生遊軍，與戰，破之，遂進圍隔城。

translations.literal: Auxiliary State General Zhu Gong'en led troops in hidden ambush, encountered Tiansheng's reconnaissance force, fought them, routed them, and then advanced to besiege Gecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary State General Zhu Gong'en lay in ambush with his troops, met Tiansheng's reconnaissance force, defeated them, and then advanced to besiege Gecheng.

sentences.zh: 天生引魏兵步騎萬餘人來戰，虎奮擊，大破之，俘斬二千餘人。

translations.literal: Tiansheng led more than ten thousand Wei infantry and cavalry to battle; Hu fought fiercely, routed them utterly, and captured and killed more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng brought more than ten thousand Northern Wei infantry and cavalry to fight; Cao Hu struck vigorously and routed them completely, capturing and killing more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 明日，攻拔隔城，斬其襄城太守帛烏祝，復俘斬二千餘人。

translations.literal: The next day they stormed and took Gecheng, beheaded its Xiangcheng prefect Bo Wuzhu, and again captured and killed more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they stormed and captured Gecheng, executed Xiangcheng prefect Bo Wuzhu, and captured and killed more than two thousand more.

sentences.zh: 天生棄平氏城走。

translations.literal: Tiansheng abandoned Pingshi city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng abandoned Pingshi and fled.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達侵魏；

translations.literal: Chen Xianda raided Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda launched a raid into Northern Wei territory;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏遣豫州刺史拓跋斤將兵拒之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Wei sent Regional Inspector of Yu Province Tuoba Jin to lead troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Northern Wei sent Regional Inspector of Yu Province Tuoba Jin with troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏主如靈泉池；

translations.literal: On yichou, the Wei ruler went to Spirit Spring Pool;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Northern Wei emperor went to Spirit Spring Pool;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，如方山；

translations.literal: On dingmao, he went to Fang Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he went to Fang Mountain;

sentences.zh: 己巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On jisi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魏築城於醴陽，陳顯達攻拔之，進攻沘陽。

translations.literal: Wei built a fort at Liyang; Chen Xianda stormed and took it, and advanced to attack Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei built a fort at Liyang; Chen Xianda captured it and advanced to attack Biyang.

sentences.zh: 城中將士皆欲出戰，鎮將韋珍曰：「彼初至氣銳，未可與爭，且共堅守，待其力攻疲弊，然後擊之。」

translations.literal: All the officers and soldiers in the city wished to go out and fight; the garrison commander Wei Zhen said, "They have just arrived and their spirit is keen—we must not contend with them. Let us all hold firm and wait until they grow weary from attacking; then strike them."
translations.idiomatic: The city's officers and soldiers all wanted to sally forth; garrison commander Wei Zhen said, "They have just arrived full of fight—we should not meet them head-on. Hold the walls together, wait until their assault wears them down, and then counterattack."

sentences.zh: 乃憑城拒戰，旬有二日，珍夜開門掩擊，顯達還。

translations.literal: Thereupon they relied on the walls to resist; after twelve days, Zhen opened the gate by night for a surprise attack, and Xianda withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They held the walls and fought on the defensive; after twelve days Zhen opened the gate by night and struck by surprise, and Xianda withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲午，以宕昌王梁彌承為河、涼二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiawu, King of Dangchang Liang Micheng was made regional inspector of He and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiawu, King of Dangchang Liang Micheng was appointed regional inspector of He and Liang provinces.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，魏主如靈泉池，遂如方山；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, the Wei ruler went to Spirit Spring Pool, then went to Fang Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou the Northern Wei emperor went to Spirit Spring Pool and then to Fang Mountain;

sentences.zh: 己亥，還宮。

translations.literal: On jihai, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬寅，上如琅邪城講武。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renyin, the emperor went to Langya city to review troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renyin the emperor went to Langya city for a military review.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，魏淮南靖王佗卒。

translations.literal: On guimao, Prince Huainan Jing of Wei, Tuo, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Prince Huainan the Tranquil of Northern Wei, Tuo, died.

sentences.zh: 魏主方享宗廟，始薦，聞之，為廢祭，臨視哀慟。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was just performing the ancestral temple sacrifice, at the first offering, when he heard of it; he therefore canceled the rites, went to view the body, and grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor was performing the ancestral sacrifice, at the first offering, when he heard the news; he canceled the ceremony, went to view the body, and mourned with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，立冬，初臨太極殿讀時令。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, at the beginning of winter, for the first time he went to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to read the seasonal ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, at the onset of winter the emperor for the first time went to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to announce the seasonal ordinances.

sentences.zh: 閏月，辛酉，以尚書僕射王奐為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on xinyou, Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Huan was made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on xinyou, Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Huan was appointed General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主如靈泉池；

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Wei ruler went to Spirit Spring Pool;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Northern Wei emperor went to Spirit Spring Pool;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，還宮。

translations.literal: On guiyou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，柔然伊吾戍主高羔子帥眾三千以城附魏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Yiwu garrison commander of Rouran, Gao Gaozi, led three thousand men in surrendering the city to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Gao Gaozi, garrison commander of Yiwu for Rouran, led three thousand men in surrendering the city to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 上以中外谷帛至賤，用尚書右丞江夏李珪之議，出上庫錢五千萬及出諸州錢，皆令糴買。

translations.literal: Because grain and cloth inside and outside the court had fallen extremely cheap, following the proposal of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Li Guizhi of Jiangxia, he disbursed fifty million cash from the upper treasury and cash from the various provinces, all to buy grain in.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain and cloth prices had fallen very low throughout the realm, the emperor, following the proposal of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Li Guizhi of Jiangxia, released fifty million cash from the central treasury plus funds from the provinces to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 西陵戍主杜元懿建言：「吳興無秋，會稽豐登，商旅往來，倍多常歲。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Xiling, Du Yuanyi, proposed: "Wuxing had no harvest, Kuaiji had a bountiful crop, and travelers going back and forth were more than double an ordinary year.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanyi, garrison commander of Xiling, proposed: "Wuxing had no harvest while Kuaiji enjoyed a bumper crop, and merchant traffic was more than double the usual volume.

sentences.zh: 西陵牛埭稅，官格日三千五百；

translations.literal: The Xiling ox-dam toll, by the official quota, was thirty-five hundred per day;
translations.idiomatic: The official quota for the Xiling ox-dam toll was thirty-five hundred per day;

sentences.zh: 如臣所見，日可增倍。

translations.literal: In this humble servant's view, it could be doubled each day.
translations.idiomatic: In my view the daily rate could be doubled.

sentences.zh: 並浦陽南北津、柳浦四埭，乞為官領攝一年，格外可長四百許萬。

translations.literal: Together with the north and south fords of Puyang and the four dams of Liupu, I beg to supervise them on the state's behalf for one year; beyond the quota an additional four million or so could be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the north and south crossings at Puyang and the four dams at Liupu, I ask to administer them on the state's behalf for one year; beyond the regular quota some four million extra could be collected.

sentences.zh: 西陵戍前檢稅，無妨戍事；

translations.literal: Tax collection in front of the Xiling garrison would not hinder garrison duties;
translations.idiomatic: At Xiling I would inspect tolls myself without interfering with garrison duties;

sentences.zh: 餘三埭自舉腹心。」

translations.literal: For the other three dams I would personally recommend trusted men."
translations.idiomatic: for the other three dams I would appoint my own trusted men."

sentences.zh: 上以其事下會稽，會稽行事吳郡顧憲之議以為：「始立牛埭之意，非苟逼蹴以取稅也，乃以風濤迅險，濟急利物耳。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the matter down to Kuaiji; Acting Administrator of Kuaiji Gu Xianzhi of Wu Commandery argued: "The original purpose in establishing the ox dams was not to squeeze travelers merely for tax revenue, but because wind and waves were swift and dangerous, to aid urgent crossings and benefit travelers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the matter to Kuaiji, where Acting Administrator Gu Xianzhi of Wu Commandery argued: "The ox dams were not established merely to press travelers for revenue, but to help people cross when winds and waves made the river treacherous.

sentences.zh: 後之監領者不達其本，各務己功，或禁遏佗道，或空稅江行，案吳興頻歲失稔，今茲尤甚，去之從豐，良田饑棘。

translations.literal: Later overseers did not understand the root purpose, each pursued his own achievement, some blocking alternate routes, some levying tolls on empty river passage; as for Wuxing, in successive years harvests have failed, and this year is especially severe—those who leave do so for plenty, while good fields become famine thorn-land.
translations.idiomatic: Later supervisors lost sight of that purpose and pursued their own profit, sometimes blocking alternate routes or taxing empty river traffic. Wuxing has suffered failed harvests year after year, and this year is worse than ever—people flee toward abundance while fertile fields turn to wasteland.

sentences.zh: 埭司責稅，依格弗降，舊格新減，尚未議登，格外加倍，將以何術！

translations.literal: The dam offices demand taxes and, following the quota, will not reduce them—the old quota has only just been reduced, and an increase has not yet been deliberated—doubling beyond the quota: by what means is this to be done!
translations.idiomatic: The dam offices still collect tolls at the full official rate—rates were only just cut and no increase has even been discussed—so how can they possibly double the quota!

sentences.zh: 皇慈恤隱，振廩蠲調；

translations.literal: Imperial benevolence pities the distressed, relieves granaries and remits levies;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial compassion has eased distress, opened granaries, and remitted taxes;

sentences.zh: 而元懿幸災榷利，重增困瘼，人而不仁，古今共疾！

translations.literal: yet Yuanyi profits from the disaster by monopolizing gain, greatly adding to affliction—one who is human yet lacks benevolence is despised alike in ancient and modern times!
translations.idiomatic: yet Yuanyi would profit from others' misfortune and pile new burdens on the afflicted—a man who is human in form but not in heart is condemned in every age!

sentences.zh: 若事不副言，懼貽譴詰，必百方侵苦，為公賈怨。

translations.literal: If the results do not match his words, he will fear reprimand and surely torment people in every way, bringing resentment upon Your Lordship.
translations.idiomatic: If results fail to match his promises he will fear reprimand and surely squeeze the people by every means, bringing blame upon your administration.

sentences.zh: 元懿稟性苛刻，已彰往效；

translations.literal: Yuanyi's nature is harsh and exacting, as past results have already shown;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi's harsh character has already been proved by past experience;

sentences.zh: 任以物土，譬以狼將羊，其所欲舉腹心，亦當虎而冠耳。

translations.literal: to entrust him with goods and land is like setting a wolf to guard sheep; the trusted men he wishes to appoint would likewise be tigers wearing caps.
translations.idiomatic: to put him in charge of revenue is like setting a wolf to guard sheep, and the trusted men he would appoint would be wolves in men's clothing as well.

sentences.zh: 書云：『與其有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣。』

translations.literal: The Classic says: "Rather than have a minister who amasses wealth, better have a minister who steals.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, "Better a thieving minister than one who amasses wealth.'

sentences.zh: 此言盜公為損蓋微，斂民所害乃大也。

translations.literal: This saying means that stealing from the public causes only slight loss, while extracting from the people causes great harm.
translations.idiomatic: The point is that theft from the state does slight harm, while extraction from the people does great harm.

sentences.zh: 愚又以便宜者，蓋謂便於公，宜於民也。

translations.literal: I further hold that what is called expedient should mean convenient for the state and suitable for the people.
translations.idiomatic: I also hold that what is called expedient should mean what benefits the state and suits the people.

sentences.zh: 竊見頃之言便宜者，非能於民力之外，用天分地；

translations.literal: I have privately observed that those who lately speak of expedient measures are not able, beyond the people's strength, to use Heaven's allotment of land;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that those who lately propose expedient measures are not finding resources beyond what the people's strength allows;

sentences.zh: 率皆即日不宜於民，方來不便於公。

translations.literal: they are generally at once unsuitable for the people, and in the future inconvenient for the state.
translations.idiomatic: they generally harm the people at once and will burden the state hereafter.

sentences.zh: 名與實反，有乖政體。

translations.literal: Name and reality are reversed—this is at odds with sound governance.
translations.idiomatic: Name and reality are reversed—this is at odds with sound governance.

sentences.zh: 凡如此等，誠宜深察。」

translations.literal: For all such cases, deep scrutiny is truly appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as these truly call for careful scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 上納之而止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this and stopped the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 魏主訪群臣以安民之術。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler asked the ministers about methods to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor asked his ministers for methods of pacifying the people.

sentences.zh: 秘書丞李彪上封事，以為：「豪貴之家，奢僭過度，第宅車服，宜為之等制。」

translations.literal: Secretary Director Li Biao submitted a sealed memorial, arguing: "In households of the powerful and noble, extravagance and presumption exceed bounds; residences, carriages, and raiment should be subject to graded regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Li Biao submitted a sealed memorial, arguing: "Among the powerful and noble, extravagance exceeded all bounds, and graded regulations should govern residences, carriages, and dress."

sentences.zh: 「又，國之興亡，在塚嗣之善惡；

translations.literal: " Further, a state's rise and fall depends on the good or evil of the heir;
translations.idiomatic: " Further, whether a state rises or falls depends on the character of the heir;

sentences.zh: 塚嗣之善惡，在教諭之得失。

translations.literal: the good or evil of the heir depends on the success or failure of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: and the character of the heir depends on the quality of his education.

sentences.zh: 高宗文成皇帝嘗謂群臣曰：『朕始學之日，年尚幼沖，情未能專；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong Wencheng once said to the ministers: "When I first began to study, I was still very young in years and my mind could not concentrate;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng once told his ministers, "When I first began my studies I was very young and unable to concentrate;

sentences.zh: 既臨萬機，不遑溫習。

translations.literal: once I assumed the myriad affairs of state, I had no leisure to warm over my studies.
translations.idiomatic: once I assumed the throne I had no time to keep up my studies.

sentences.zh: 今日思之。

translations.literal: Thinking of it today,
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on it now,

sentences.zh: 豈唯予咎，抑亦師傅之不勤。』

translations.literal: is this not only my fault, but also the tutors' lack of diligence?'
translations.idiomatic: the fault is not mine alone, but also my tutors' failure to teach diligently.'

sentences.zh: 尚書李言斤免冠謝。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Yanjin removed his cap and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Yanjin removed his cap and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 此近事之可鑒者也。

translations.literal: This is a recent matter that can serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: This recent episode offers a clear warning.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜准古立師傅之官，以訓導太子。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that one should follow antiquity in establishing tutorship offices to instruct and guide the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the court follow ancient precedent by establishing tutorship offices to instruct the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 「又，漢置常平倉以救匱乏。

translations.literal: " Further, the Han established Ever-Normal Granaries to relieve scarcity.
translations.idiomatic: " Further, the Han dynasty established Ever-Normal Granaries to relieve want.

sentences.zh: 去歲京師不稔，移民就豐，既廢營生，困而後達，又於國體，實有虛損。

translations.literal: Last year the capital region had a poor harvest; people were moved to areas of plenty, abandoning their livelihoods, reaching only after hardship, and this in fact hollowed out the state's substance.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the capital region had a poor harvest; people were relocated to fertile areas, abandoning their livelihoods and reaching hardship before relief, which in truth weakened the state.

sentences.zh: 曷若豫儲倉粟，安而給之，豈不愈於驅督老弱餬口千里之外哉！

translations.literal: How much better to store grain in advance and supply it peacefully—is this not superior to driving the old and weak to feed themselves a thousand li away!
translations.idiomatic: How much better to store grain in advance and distribute it at home—is that not preferable to driving the old and weak a thousand li to scrape a living elsewhere!

sentences.zh: 宜析州郡常調九分之二，京師度支歲用之餘，各立官司，年豐糴粟積之於倉，儉則加私之二糶之於人。

translations.literal: One should allocate two parts in nine from the regular levies of provinces and commanderies, and from the capital's annual surplus after expenses, establish separate offices; in years of plenty buy grain and store it in granaries, and in years of scarcity sell it to the people at two parts above the private price.
translations.idiomatic: Two-ninths of the regular provincial levies and the capital's annual surplus should be set aside under dedicated offices; in years of plenty grain should be purchased and stored, and in years of scarcity sold to the people at a modest markup.

sentences.zh: 如此，民必力田以取官絹，積財以取官粟。

translations.literal: In this way the people will surely labor in the fields to obtain official silk and accumulate wealth to obtain official grain.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people will work the fields to earn official silk and save to buy official grain.

sentences.zh: 年登則常積，歲凶則直給。

translations.literal: In years of plenty there will be regular accumulation; in years of famine there will be direct distribution.
translations.idiomatic: In good years grain will accumulate; in bad years it will be distributed directly.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，谷積而人足，雖災不為害矣。」

translations.literal: Within a few years grain will be stored and the people provided for, and even disaster will do no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years stores will fill and the people will be secure, so that even famine will do little harm."

sentences.zh: 「又，宜於河表七州人中，擢其門才，引令赴闕，依中州官比，隨能序之。

translations.literal: " Further, among the people of the seven provinces south of the Yellow River one should select men of talent from good families, summon them to court, and rank them according to ability by comparison with Central Province offices.
translations.idiomatic: " Further, talented men from good families among the seven provinces south of the Yellow River should be selected, summoned to court, and ranked according to ability on the same scale as Central Province offices.

sentences.zh: 一可以廣聖朝均新舊之義，一可以懷江、漢歸有道之情。」

translations.literal: This would both broaden the sacred court's principle of treating old and new alike, and win over the feelings of those along the Yangtze and Han who would return to the Way."
translations.idiomatic: This would both extend the court's principle of treating old and new subjects equally and win over the hearts of the people along the Yangtze and Han who wish to submit to a righteous ruler."

sentences.zh: 「又，父子兄弟，異體同氣；

translations.literal: " Further, fathers and sons and brothers, though different in body, share the same breath;
translations.idiomatic: " Further, fathers and sons and brothers, though separate in body, share one breath of life;

sentences.zh: 罪不相及，乃君上之厚恩。

translations.literal: that crimes do not extend to one another is the sovereign's great grace.
translations.idiomatic: that punishment does not extend from one to another is the sovereign's great mercy.

sentences.zh: 至於憂懼相連，固自然之恆理也。

translations.literal: That worry and fear should be linked is, after all, the constant principle of nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that kin should share one another's worry and fear is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 無情之人，父兄繫獄，子弟無慘惕之容；

translations.literal: Yet heartless men, when fathers and elder brothers are imprisoned, show no look of grief and fear on the faces of sons and younger brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Yet among the heartless, when fathers and elder brothers are imprisoned, sons and younger brothers show no grief or fear;

sentences.zh: 子弟逃刑，父兄無愧恧之色；

translations.literal: when sons and younger brothers flee punishment, fathers and elder brothers show no look of shame;
translations.idiomatic: when sons and younger brothers flee justice, fathers and elder brothers show no shame;

sentences.zh: 宴安榮位，游從自若，車馬衣冠，不變華飾；

translations.literal: they feast in ease and honor, roam and associate as they please, and their carriages, horses, and raiment remain unchanged in splendor;
translations.idiomatic: they feast at ease in honored office, go about as before, and their carriages, horses, and dress remain as splendid as ever;

sentences.zh: 骨肉之恩，豈當然也！

translations.literal: can this be what is proper to the bond of flesh and blood!
translations.idiomatic: can this be what flesh and blood ought to mean!

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為父兄有犯，宜令子弟素服肉袒，詣闕請罪。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that when fathers and elder brothers commit offenses, sons and younger brothers should be ordered to wear plain white and bare the upper body, and go to court to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that when fathers and elder brothers commit offenses, their sons and younger brothers should wear plain white, bare the upper body, and come to court to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 子弟有坐，宜令父兄露板引咎，乞解所司；

translations.literal: When sons and younger brothers are guilty, fathers and elder brothers should expose a placard acknowledging fault and beg to be relieved of office;
translations.idiomatic: When sons and younger brothers are guilty, fathers and elder brothers should post a public confession and ask to be relieved of office;

sentences.zh: 若職任必要，不宜許者，慰勉留之。

translations.literal: if the post is necessary and dismissal is not appropriate, they should be comforted and encouraged to remain.
translations.idiomatic: if the post is indispensable and dismissal is not feasible, they should be consoled and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 如此，足以敦厲凡薄，使人知所恥矣。」

translations.literal: In this way it would be enough to encourage and discipline the common and shallow, and make people know shame."
translations.idiomatic: In this way the court could strengthen public morals and teach people what shame means."

sentences.zh: 「又，朝臣遭親喪者，假滿赴職。

translations.literal: " Further, when court ministers suffer the death of a parent, once mourning leave ends they return to office.
translations.idiomatic: " Further, when court ministers lose a parent, once mourning leave ends they return to office.

sentences.zh: 衣錦乘軒，從郊廟之祀；

translations.literal: Dressed in brocade, riding in curtained carriages, they follow the suburban and temple sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in brocade and riding in curtained carriages, they attend suburban and temple sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 鳴玉垂絲委，同慶賜之燕。

translations.literal: Jade pendants sounding, sash cords hanging loose, they join the feasts of congratulatory bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Their jade pendants chime and sash cords trail as they attend the court's celebratory banquets and gift-giving feasts.

sentences.zh: 傷人子之道，虧天地之經。

translations.literal: This injures the Way of being a son, and violates the constant principle of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: This wounds the duty of a filial son and violates the fundamental order of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 愚謂凡遭大父母、父母喪者，皆聽終服；

translations.literal: Your humble servant holds that all who suffer the death of a grandparent or parent should be permitted to complete the full mourning period;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that all who lose a grandparent or parent should be allowed to observe the full mourning period;

sentences.zh: 若無其人，職業有曠者，則優旨慰喻，起令視事，但綜司出納、敷奏而已，國之吉慶，一令無預。

translations.literal: If there is no one else and the office would otherwise stand vacant, then with gracious edicts offer comfort and persuasion, raise them to resume duty, but only to oversee receipts and disbursements and present memorials—nothing more; as for the state's auspicious celebrations, let them have no part at all.
translations.idiomatic: If no substitute exists and the post would go unfilled, the throne should send a gracious edict of consolation and recall the mourner to office—but only to manage accounts and present memorials. He should take no part whatever in the state's joyous ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 其軍旅之警，墨縗從役，雖愆於禮，事所宜行也。」

translations.literal: When there is military alarm, to serve in black mourning garb, though a breach of ritual, is what circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: In times of military emergency, serving in simplified black mourning dress—though a lapse from proper ritual—is what circumstances demand."

sentences.zh: 魏主皆從之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler adopted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor accepted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 由是公私豐贍，雖時有水旱，而民不困窮。

translations.literal: From this both public and private stores were abundant; though there were at times flood and drought, the people did not fall into destitution.
translations.idiomatic: From this both the state and private households grew prosperous; and though flood and drought occurred from time to time, the people did not suffer want.

sentences.zh: 魏遣兵擊百濟，為百濟所敗。

translations.literal: Wei sent troops to attack Baekje and was defeated by Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei sent troops against Baekje and was defeated by them.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明七年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 7 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 7 (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元四八九年）

translations.literal: jisi, the year 489 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jisi, corresponding to 489 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏主祀南郊，始備大駕。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sacrificed at the Southern Suburb and for the first time deployed the full imperial carriage train.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice and for the first time employed the full imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，臨川獻王映卒。

translations.literal: On renxu, Prince Xian of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Prince Xian of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, died.

sentences.zh: 初，上為鎮西長史，主簿王晏以傾諂為上所親，自是常在上府。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won the emperor's favor through fawning flattery; from then on he was constantly at the prince's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won his favor through sycophantic flattery and thereafter remained constantly at his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 上為太子，晏為中庶子。

translations.literal: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan became Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan was made Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上之得罪於太祖也，晏稱疾自疏。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan pleaded illness and kept his distance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan feigned illness and distanced himself.

sentences.zh: 及即位，為丹陽尹，意任如舊，朝夕進見，議論朝事；

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor's trust in him was as before, and he was received morning and evening to discuss court affairs;
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor trusted him as before and received him morning and evening to discuss affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 自豫章王嶷及王儉皆降意接之。

translations.literal: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all lowered themselves to receive him graciously.
translations.idiomatic: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all showed deference in receiving him.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，出為江州刺史；

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, he was sent out as Inspector of Jiang Province;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, he was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province;

sentences.zh: 晏不願外出，復留為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Yan did not wish to go out on assignment and was again retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not wish to leave the capital and was kept on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，立皇子子岳為臨賀王，子峻為廣漢王，子琳為宣城王，子鈱為義安王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁丑，魏主詔曰：「升樓散物以繼百姓，至使人馬騰踐，多有傷毀；
