translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou, the Wei ruler issued an edict saying, "Ascending towers to scatter goods to succor the people has come to the point where men and horses trample and leap about, and many are injured and harmed;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou, the Northern Wei emperor issued an edict: "The custom of ascending towers to scatter goods for the people has led to such crowding and trampling by men and horses that many are injured;

sentences.zh: 今可斷之，以本所費之物，賜老疾貧獨者。」

translations.literal: henceforth this may be stopped, and the goods that would have been spent on it should be given to the aged, the sick, the poor, and those without family."
translations.idiomatic: hereafter it shall cease, and the goods that would have been used for it shall be given directly to the aged, the sick, the poor, and those living alone."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏主如靈泉池，遂如方山；

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Wei ruler went to the Lingquan Pool, then proceeded to Mount Fang;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Northern Wei emperor went to the Lingquan Pool and then to Mount Fang;

sentences.zh: 己丑，還宮。

translations.literal: On jichou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 上優禮南昌文憲公王儉，詔三日一還朝，尚書令史出外諮事。

translations.literal: The emperor treated with exceptional honor Duke Wenxian of Nanchang, Wang Jian, ordering him to return to court once every three days, with clerks of the Masters of Writing going out to consult him on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accorded exceptional honors to Duke Wenxian of Nanchang, Wang Jian, ordering him to attend court once every three days while clerks of the Masters of Writing came out to consult him on business.

sentences.zh: 上猶以往來煩數，復詔儉還尚書下省，月聽十日出外。

translations.literal: The emperor still considered the coming and going too frequent, and again ordered Jian to return to the lower offices of the Masters of Writing, permitting him to go out only ten days each month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still found the back-and-forth too burdensome and again ordered Jian to remain at the lower offices of the Masters of Writing, allowing him to go out only ten days a month.

sentences.zh: 儉固求解選。

translations.literal: Jian firmly requested release from personnel selection duties.
translations.idiomatic: Jian repeatedly asked to be relieved of his duties in personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 詔改中書監，參掌選事。

translations.literal: An edict changed his post to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, with shared charge of selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred him to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat with shared responsibility for personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙巳，儉卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yisi, Wang Jian died.

sentences.zh: 王晏既領選，權行台閣，與儉頗不平。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, having taken charge of selection, wielded the authority of the Secretariat and was on rather poor terms with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, now in charge of personnel selection, exercised the powers of the Secretariat and was on bad terms with Jian.

sentences.zh: 禮官欲依王導，謚儉為文獻。

translations.literal: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and give Jian the posthumous title Literary Paragon.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and posthumously name Jian Literary Paragon.

sentences.zh: 晏啟上曰：「導乃得此謚；

translations.literal: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Dao deserved this posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Wang Dao deserved that posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 但宋氏以來，不加異姓。」

translations.literal: since the Song dynasty, such titles have not been granted to those of a different surname;"
translations.idiomatic: since the Song, such titles have not been granted to men of a different surname;"

sentences.zh: 出，謂親人曰：「『平頭憲』事已行矣。」

translations.literal: After leaving, he told his intimates, "The affair of the 'truncated Xian' has already been settled."
translations.idiomatic: After leaving, he told his intimates, "The affair of the 'Flat-Xian' title is already settled."

sentences.zh: 徐湛之之死也，其孫孝嗣在孕得免。

translations.literal: When Xu Zhanzhi was put to death, his grandson Xiaosi, still in the womb, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Zhanzhi was executed, his grandson Xiaosi, still unborn, was spared.

sentences.zh: 八歲，襲爵枝江縣公，尚宋康樂公主。

translations.literal: At eight years of age he inherited the title Duke of Zhijiang County and married Princess Kangle of Song.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he inherited the title Duke of Zhijiang County and married Princess Kangle of Song.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，孝嗣為御史中丞，風儀端簡。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Xiaosi was Palace Censor-in-Chief, dignified and restrained in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Xiaosi served as Palace Censor-in-Chief, distinguished by his dignified and restrained bearing.

sentences.zh: 王儉謂人曰：「徐孝嗣將來必為宰相。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian said to others, "Xu Xiaosi will surely become chief minister in the future."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian told others, "Xu Xiaosi will surely become chief minister one day."

sentences.zh: 上嘗問儉：「誰可繼卿者？」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Jian, "Who can succeed you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Jian, "Who can succeed you?"

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「臣東都之日，其在徐孝嗣乎！」

translations.literal: Jian replied, "When I go east to the capital, will it not be Xu Xiaosi!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "When I depart for the eastern capital, will it not be Xu Xiaosi!"

sentences.zh: 儉卒，孝嗣時為吳興太守，征為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Xiaosi was then Administrator of Wuxing and was summoned to be Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian died, Xiaosi was serving as Administrator of Wuxing and was summoned to be Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主祭方澤。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Wei ruler sacrificed at the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Northern Wei emperor performed the sacrifice at the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 上欲用領軍王奐為尚書令，以問王晏。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Wang Yan about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏與奐不相能，對曰：「柳世隆有勳望，恐不宜在奐後。」

translations.literal: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has merit and prestige; I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."
translations.idiomatic: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has both merit and prestige; it would hardly be fitting to rank him below Huan."

sentences.zh: 甲子，以尚書左僕射柳世隆為尚書令，王奐為左僕射。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Left Vice Director Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁亥，上如琅邪城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dinghai, the emperor went to Langya City.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dinghai, the emperor went to Langya City.

sentences.zh: 魏懷朔鎮將汝陰靈王天賜，長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史南安惠王楨，皆坐髒當死。

translations.literal: The Wei General of Huaishuo Garrison, Spirit King of Runan, Tiansi, and the Grand General of Chang'an Garrison and Inspector of Yong Province, Kind King of Nan'an, Zhen, were both convicted of corruption and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei general of Huaishuo Garrison, Spirit Prince of Runan Tiansi, and the grand general of Chang'an Garrison and Inspector of Yong Province, Kind Prince of Nan'an Zhen, were both convicted of corruption and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 馮太后及魏主臨皇信堂，引見王公，太后令曰：「卿等以為當存親以毀令邪？

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng and the Wei ruler attended at the Huangxin Hall and summoned the princes and dukes to audience. The empress dowager ordered, "Do you think kinship should be preserved and the law destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng and the Northern Wei emperor attended at the Huangxin Hall and summoned the princes and dukes for audience. The empress dowager said, "Do you think kinship should be preserved at the cost of destroying the law?

sentences.zh: 當滅親以明法邪？」

translations.literal: Or should kinship be destroyed to clarify the law?"
translations.idiomatic: Or should kinship be set aside to uphold the law?"

sentences.zh: 群臣皆言：「二王，景穆皇帝之子，宜蒙矜恕。」

translations.literal: All the ministers said, "The two princes are sons of Emperor Jingmu and ought to receive compassionate pardon."
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers said, "The two princes are sons of Emperor Jingmu and ought to receive clemency."

sentences.zh: 太后不應。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager made no reply.

sentences.zh: 魏主乃下詔，稱：「二王所犯難恕，而太皇太后追惟高宗孔懷之恩；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler then issued an edict, stating, "The crimes of the two princes are hard to forgive, yet the Grand Empress Dowager recalls the deep brotherly affection of Emperor Gaozong;
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor then issued an edict stating, "The crimes of the two princes are hard to forgive, yet the Grand Empress Dowager recalls the deep brotherly bond of Emperor Gaozong;

sentences.zh: 且南安王事母孝謹，聞於中外，並特免死，削奪官爵，禁錮終身。」

translations.literal: moreover Prince Nan'an served his mother with filial care and was known within and without; both are specially spared death, stripped of office and rank, and imprisoned for life."
translations.idiomatic: moreover Prince Nan'an served his mother with filial devotion, as was known throughout the realm; both are specially spared death, stripped of office and rank, and imprisoned for life."

sentences.zh: 初，魏朝聞楨貪暴，遣中散閭文祖詣長安察之，文祖受楨賂，為之隱；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Wei court heard that Zhen was greedy and violent, it sent Palace Attendant Lü Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate; Wenzu accepted bribes from Zhen and concealed the truth for him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Wei court heard that Zhen was greedy and brutal, it sent Palace Attendant Lü Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate; Wenzu accepted bribes from Zhen and covered up his crimes;

sentences.zh: 事覺，文祖亦抵罪。

translations.literal: when the matter came to light, Wenzu also was punished for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: when the matter came to light, Wenzu was punished as well.

sentences.zh: 馮太后謂群臣曰：「文祖前自謂廉，今竟犯法。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng said to the ministers, "Wenzu formerly declared himself incorrupt, yet in the end he violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng said to the ministers, "Wenzu once declared himself incorrupt, yet in the end he broke the law.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，人心信不可知！」

translations.literal: Judging by this, the human heart truly cannot be known!"
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see that the human heart truly cannot be known!"

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「古有待放之臣。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "In antiquity there were officials who awaited dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In antiquity there were officials who awaited dismissal.

sentences.zh: 卿等自審不勝貪心者，聽辭位歸第。」

translations.literal: If you yourselves judge that you cannot overcome greed, you are permitted to resign your posts and return home."
translations.idiomatic: If any of you judge yourselves unable to overcome greed, you may resign your posts and return home."

sentences.zh: 宰官、中散慕容契進曰：「小人之心無常，而帝王之法有常；

translations.literal: Director of Officials and Palace Attendant Murong Qi advanced and said, "The hearts of petty men are inconstant, while the laws of emperors and kings are constant;
translations.idiomatic: Director of Officials and Palace Attendant Murong Qi stepped forward and said, "The hearts of petty men are inconstant, while the laws of emperors and kings are constant;

sentences.zh: 以無常之心奉有常之法，非所克堪，乞從退黜。」

translations.literal: to serve constant law with an inconstant heart is more than one can bear—I beg to be dismissed and removed."
translations.idiomatic: to serve constant law with an inconstant heart is more than I can bear—I beg to be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「契知心不可常，則知貪之可惡矣，何必求退！」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "Qi, knowing that the heart cannot be constant, you already know how hateful greed is—why must you seek dismissal!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Qi, if you know the heart cannot be constant, then you already know how hateful greed is—why seek dismissal!"

sentences.zh: 遷宰官令。

translations.literal: He promoted him to Director of Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Qi to Director of Officials.

sentences.zh: 契，白曜之弟子也。

translations.literal: Qi was a nephew of Bai Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a nephew of Bai Yao.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅，魏主如靈泉池。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the Wei ruler went to the Lingquan Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the Northern Wei emperor went to the Lingquan Pool.

sentences.zh: 魏主使群臣議，「久與齊絕，今欲通使，何如？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler had the ministers discuss the question, "We have long been cut off from Qi; now we wish to exchange envoys—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor had his ministers discuss the question: "We have long been cut off from Qi; now we wish to exchange envoys—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 尚書游明根曰：「朝廷不遣使者，又築醴陽深入彼境，皆直在蕭賾。

translations.literal: Minister You Minggen said, "That the court sent no envoys, and also built Liyang deep in their territory—the fault lies entirely with Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Minister You Minggen said, "That our court sent no envoys, and that we built Liyang deep in their territory—the fault lies entirely with Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 不復追使，不亦可乎！」

translations.literal: Not to send envoys again—would that not also be acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: Surely we need not send envoys again!"

sentences.zh: 魏主從之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥，遣兼員外散騎常侍邢產等來聘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yihai, he sent Acting Supernumerary Palace Attendant Xing Chan and others on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yihai, he sent Acting Supernumerary Palace Attendant Xing Chan and others on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 九月，魏出宮人以賜北鎮人貧無妻者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wei released palace women to be given to poor men of the northern garrisons who had no wives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Northern Wei released palace women to be given to poor men of the northern garrisons who had no wives.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己未，魏安豐匡王猛卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiwei, Prince Kuang of Anfeng, Meng, of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiwei, Prince Kuang of Anfeng, Meng, of Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙子，魏河東王苟頹卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, Prince of Hedong, Gou Tui, of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, Prince of Hedong Gou Tui of Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 平南參軍顏幼明等聘於魏。

translations.literal: Staff Officer of the Army of the South Yan Youming and others went on a friendly mission to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer of the Army of the South Yan Youming and others paid a diplomatic visit to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以尚書令尉元為司徒，左僕射穆亮為司空。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Yuan as Minister over the Masses and Left Vice Director Mu Liang as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei appointed Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Yuan as Minister over the Masses and Left Vice Director Mu Liang as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷自以地位隆重，深懷退素，是歲，啟求還第；

translations.literal: Prince Liao of Yuzhang, considering his position weighty and eminent, deeply cherished withdrawal and simplicity; that year he memorialized requesting to return to his residence;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liao of Yuzhang, considering his position too weighty and eminent, deeply wished to live in modest retirement; that year he memorialized asking to return to his residence;

sentences.zh: 上令其世子子廉代鎮東府。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his heir Zilian to take his place and garrison the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his heir Zilian to take his place and garrison the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事張緒領揚州中正，長沙王晃屬用吳興聞人邕為州議曹，緒不許。

translations.literal: Household Steward of the Heir Apparent Zhang Xu held the post of Yang Province Rectifier; Prince Huang of Changsha wished to appoint Wenren Yong of Wuxing as Provincial Deliberation Officer, but Xu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Household Steward of the Heir Apparent Zhang Xu served as Yang Province Rectifier; Prince Huang of Changsha wished to appoint Wenren Yong of Wuxing as Provincial Deliberation Officer, but Xu refused.

sentences.zh: 晃使書佐固請，緒正色曰：「此是身家州鄉，殿下何得見逼！」

translations.literal: Huang had his clerical aide press the request firmly; Xu said sternly, "This concerns my own clan and native district—how can Your Highness press me in this way!"
translations.idiomatic: Huang had his clerical aide press the request; Xu said sternly, "This concerns my own clan and native district—how can Your Highness pressure me in this way!"

sentences.zh: 侍中江學為都官尚書。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Jiang Xue was made Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Jiang Xue was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人紀僧真得幸於上，容表有士風，請於上曰：「臣出自本縣武吏，邀逢聖時，階榮至此；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant Ji Sengzhen had won the emperor's favor; in bearing and appearance he had the air of a gentleman. He requested of the emperor, "Your servant comes from a military clerk of his home county; by encountering this sage age I have risen in honor to this point;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Attendant Ji Sengzhen had won the emperor's favor; in bearing and appearance he had the air of a gentleman. He petitioned the emperor: "I come from a military clerk in my home county; by good fortune in this sage age I have risen to such honor;

sentences.zh: 為兒昏得荀昭光女，即時無復所須，唯就陛下乞作士大夫。」

translations.literal: in arranging my son's marriage I obtained the daughter of Xun Zhaoguang, and now I lack for nothing; I ask only of Your Majesty to be made a gentleman-official."
translations.idiomatic: my son's marriage to the daughter of Xun Zhaoguang has left me wanting for nothing; I ask only that Your Majesty grant me entry among the gentry-officials."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此由江學、謝瀹，我不得措意，可自詣之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This depends on Jiang Xue and Xie Yue; I cannot decide it myself—you may go to them yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is for Jiang Xue and Xie Yue to decide; I cannot intervene—you must go to them yourself."

sentences.zh: 僧真承旨詣學，登榻坐定，學顧命左右曰：「移吾床遠客！」

translations.literal: Sengzhen followed the edict and went to Xue; he mounted the couch and sat down. Xue turned and ordered his attendants, "Move my couch away from this visitor!"
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen followed the emperor's instruction and went to Xue; he mounted the couch and sat down. Xue turned to his attendants and said, "Move my couch away from this visitor!"

sentences.zh: 僧真喪氣而退，告上曰：「士大夫故非天子所命！」

translations.literal: Sengzhen lost heart and withdrew; he told the emperor, "Gentry-official status is truly not something the Son of Heaven can command!"
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen withdrew in dejection and told the emperor, "Gentry-official standing is truly not something the Son of Heaven can bestow!"

sentences.zh: 學，湛之孫；

translations.literal: Xue was a grandson of Zhanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Xue was a grandson of Xu Zhanzhi;

sentences.zh: 瀹，朏之弟也。

translations.literal: Yue was a younger brother of Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was a younger brother of Xie Fei.

sentences.zh: 柔然別帥叱呂勤帥眾降魏。

translations.literal: A separate chieftain of Rouran, Chilüqin, led his followers in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: A Rouran sub-chieftain, Chilüqin, led his followers in surrender to Northern Wei.
